paragraphs.text: Marvin Gaye, Matt Cassel,
And Those Chiefs

frames.text: Marvin Gaye, Matt Cassel, And Those Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Y’all know Marvin Gaye, He was the greatest Motown singer ever. Singing hits like “Heard It Through The Grapevine” and “Let’s Get It On” and “Makes Me Wanna Holler”.

But one of his most unknown songs was entitled, “Ain’t That Peculiar”. It is with this song in mind that we will talk about the Kansas City Chiefs, this week. Many of you know that the Chiefs will be facing the Buffalo Bills, in Buffalo, New York this Sunday. And let’s not forget that Matt Cassel will still  be the starting quarterback for the Chiefs. . . again.

This past Monday night, we all met out at the Groove Station, in South Kansas City. It is all part of our “get out and see the City” campaign. We, Monday Niters, have been going to each other’s homes for over forty years and from now on, we will find out what the restaurant cuisine is really like. But, the point is we talked about the Chiefs’ highly-inadequate quarterback, Matt Cassel.

Ain”t it peculiar that Matt Cassel never started a college football game. That’s because he played backup to Matt Leinart and Carson Palmer at USC. Further, ain’t it peculiar that he was not a starter in the NFL, either. He gained fame by backing up New England’s Tom Brady, during an unexpected injury. So it’s begs the question....why in the hell should the Chiefs’ expect any more than a backup game, when Matt Cassel is still starting? Now, that is peculiar. But let’s move on, knowing that the Chiefs will not win unless they replace Matt Cassel. Enough said about that.

Back to the Groove Station venue. Ollie hosted us out there because he lives only a few blocks away. That’s Ollie....location, location. And the cuisine was some delicious chicken wings, backed up with a nice sports salad. And the owner shared her story with all the guys. But, we were only interested in talking about the Chiefs’ chances against lowly Buffalo. Except for a couple of us die-hards, everyone picked Buffalo over the Chiefs, especially after that high-school showing against Tony Gonzalez and the Atlanta Falcons. All the guys think that the Chiefs still have a long way to go, before winning. Thus, it is not “peculiar” that they would pick Buffalo over the “Casseled-out” Chiefs. They think that Buffalo’s defense, led by $100 million dollar man, Mario Williams, will maul the Chiefs. Even though Buffalo’s quarterback, Ryan Fitzpatrick, ain’t no better than Cassel. Now, ain’t that peculiar?
Dr. Charles Allen: Sweet revenge from last year Chiefs by 7
Paul Booker: Chiefs are not ready for prime time     Buffalo by 10
Carl Clark:  Chiefs still ain’t ready Buffalo by 7
Bubba Cleaver: Still thinks he’s at the Democratic Convention Chiefs by 7
Ike Gardner: Chiefs need another month  Buffalo by 12
Lloyd Greenfield: Another time, another day Chiefs by 3
Ollie Hubbard: Chiefs gotta do better Buffalo by 12
Jim Nunnelly: Believing in Hali, Johnson, Charles     Chiefs by 3
Ed West: No improvement from last year Buffalo by 10 national convention

paragraphs.text: Y’all remember Roberta Flack. She was quite the talk, back in the ‘60s and ‘70s. Her hit song, “Killing Me Softly”, found its way into all of our hearts and homes. But she sang another song, which is so appropriate for our “sinking fast” Chiefs. That song will be revealed after we talk a little about the New Orleans Saints, the Chiefs’ next opponent on Sunday.

First of all, the Saints came into being as an NFL expansion team, back in the late ‘60s. Their rise to Super Bowl status has been phenomenal, especially since they had a rough, rough start. Some insensitive sportswriters once called them the “Aints”, owing to their winlessness. Now years later, we all have forgotten about those lean days and nowadays, always look to the Saints to be a contender to win the NFC South Division. Routinely now, they always play well against Division opponents like Atlanta, Carolina and Tampa Bay. But as of today, the Saints have not won a game, so far, this season. Some say it is the atmosphere. Recently, the Saints found themselves deep in controversy after the well-publicized bounty scheme. That fiasco left them without their head coach, Sean Payton, for all of this season. That penalty may well explain why the Saints are off to a rough start.

But, what about the Chiefs? What can they say to explain another “shaky” beginning? What can the Chiefs do to make it all better? Actually, we, Monday Niters, believe the Saints will recover soon and start making championship plans. But not so for the Chiefs. Why is that so, you may ask. Well, this is where we talk again about Roberta Flack.

Her “other” hit song was “The Closer I Get To You”. In that song, she is happy with the progress of her rising relationship. In fact, she proudly comments that her lover makes her “see” things more clearly. Well, the “closer”  we get to the Chiefs, the more we “see” how inept, how inadequate these bunch of bums are. Starting with the coaches, the front office and their regrettable quarterback, Matt Cassel. You don’t have to “get close” to see that these Chiefs are never gonna rise up. They are never gonna win our division again. They can stay here another 50 years and it will all be same. Full of excuses. Full of  explanations. And full of crap.

And crap it is, no matter how close you get. In fact, we should start referring to them as the “Aints”. Because they aint gonna never be nothing.  So for Sunday’s game, it will be the Saints vs. the new Aints. And you don’t have to be “close” to predict the outcome. Roberta Flack would sang another song about the Chiefs. The farther I get from you, the better I seem to be.
Monday Niters, what say you?

paragraphs.text: Shakespeare, Some Common Quotes, And The Chiefs

frames.text: Shakespeare, Some Common Quotes, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: When the Chiefs are losing, we search hard for something to talk about. And since the Chiefs have won just one game, we found ourselves talking about something odd. . . William Shakespeare, the best known playwright in the English language.

Now, this genius wrote thirty eight plays and many poems, as far back as five hundred years ago. Besides the Bible, his works are quoted more than any other form of literature. His most notable plays include Macbeth, Othello, Richard III, and Midsummer Night’s Dream. And Shakespeare was quite versatile. . . having wrote comedies, histories, character studies and a lot about politics.  What would Shakespeare have said about the Chiefs? We will find out, after looking closer at Sunday’s game against the barely-alive Oakland Raiders.

First, a little about Oakland. Like the Chiefs, the Raiders were part of the old American Football League, starting way back in 1960. Right away, the Chiefs and the Raiders became rivals, playing some real close games both at Municipal Stadium and the “Black Hole”. And somewhere along the line, the games would end up with a fight or two. Commonly called the “Silver and Black”, the Raiders have struggled in recent years. But they have won three Super Bowls, way back in 1976, 1980, and 1987.

Surprisingly, they also have 13 players in the illustrious Football Hall Of Fame, in Canton, Ohio. But all that won’t matter when they come marching into Arrowhead at noon on Sunday. The Chiefs’ fans will heckle the pirate-dressed Raiders’ fans and “there will be no peace”. The Chiefs will be trying to beat their division rival because they have only beaten San Diego this year. And Oakland will be trying to remain off the bottom, where the Chiefs currently reside. So while no championship will be at stake, it promises to be a first-rate battle. Shakespeare would have spoken a special quote for this meaningless game. “To be or not to be, that is the question.”

In response, the Monday Niters actually applied many of the famous quotes from Shakespeare to their predictions. Some of them are quite creative, so please  applaud these old men for paying attention in school. Ike actually took a college class in Shakespeare. And Loyal Lloyd has acted in a Shakespeare play or two. And Congressman Cleaver has used Shakespeare as part of his many sermons. While the rest of us have unknowingly quoted Shakespeare hundreds of times. So sit back and enjoy finding out that Shakespeare is all around us, even on a Monday night, at a boring football meeting.

Ollie Hubbard, “Expectations is the root of all heartaches” Chiefs by 3
Jim Nunnelly, “All is well that ends well”. Chiefs by 7
Ed West, “Not to be, that is the answer”.  Raiders by 10

paragraphs.text: Okay, the Chiefs won one game.

It just so happened on national television and it was raining and the team we beat just happened to have won the AFC West Division last year. And for the first time in years, the Chiefs were part of the highlight reels on ESPN, as a positive. But just as sure as Todd Haley is not going to smile, the jury is still out on the Chiefs, at least the offense.  Speaking of offense, did you see Matt Cassel grab the game ball, as if he had something to do with the victory over San Diego? Make no mistake. . . that game ball should have gone to the defense, or the punt returner or the kickoff returner or Jamal Charles.  Definitely not the quarterback.
As we look ahead to Sunday, let’s see what the Monday Niters think about the upcoming game against Cleveland, in Cleveland.
DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Monday night’s win over the Chargers was NOT a fluke.  Though improvement is still needed, the Chiefs will overtake the Browns by 10 points.

THE APOSTLE PAUL BOOKER: I’m not that confident about the Chiefs, at least not yet. The Chiefs have gotten us all excited before, only to let us down. It is my firm belief that the Chiefs cannot and won’t beat Cleveland. End of story.

COOL CARL CLARK: Unlike Booker, Carl believes the Chiefs CAN beat the Browns, if for no other reason that any team can beat another team on any given Sunday.  The Chiefs played good defense but the Chiefs’ quarterback is lacking an awful lot.

CONGRESSMAN EMANUEL CLEAVER: From this point forward, the Chiefs will be measured by speed.  They got lots of speed, on the line, in the backfield, on special teams.  With that abundance of speed, they can and will beat Cleveland.

CANTANKEROUS IKE GARDNER: The only place Ike is nice to people is out at a restaurant on 63rd.  There he is treated like royalty and he eats it up. But, his distrusting dislike for the Chiefs  While everyone else is raving about the Chiefs’ defense, Ike says the “the defense let us down”. Thus, Cleveland will beat our Chiefs on Sunday, according to Ike.

LOYAL LLOYD GREENFIELD: He agrees that the win over San Diego was a fluke. But, he was glad to see the Chiefs win something. And for the record, he is backing the Chiefs this Sunday against the Browns.  Can we trust your judgement, Lloyd?

OLLIE “KNOWS EVERYTHING” HUBBARD: Ollie is happy with the Chiefs.  You know he is part of the Ike and Booker thing that goes against the Chiefs.  But this time, Ollie joins up with the believers and picks Kansas City over Cleveland.

JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY: Matt Cassel ain’t worth $60 million, y’all.  In fact, we would have killed San Diego with Brodie Croyle at quarterback.  He is drinking from wells that he didn’t dig.  But look for local writers and broadcasters to continue to make hi m an “unhung hero”. The only thing that didn’t work for the Chiefs was the offense. And guess who was the quarterback.  Get rid of him and the Chiefs will soar.  But, special teams are enough to beat Cleveland on Sunday.

EASY ED WEST: Joining the believers is Ed West.  He flip-flops back and forth sometimes. But, this time, Ed is onto something. He thinks the Chiefs are young, hungry and motivated on both offense and defense.  Thus, his vote goes to the Chiefs to outclass Crennel’s old team, the Browns.

ERIC “ERICA’S DAD” WESSON: There is an ole’ sayin’ “Even a hobo gets lucky and gets a steak every now and then if he hangs out in the right places.” That was what I was thinking in the Chiefs Monday victory, but it will be short lived.  The bottom line is the Chiefs lack the offensive players to be a household name. They won’t be able to score enough to beat Cleveland. Season record 4-12.

FINAL NOTE:  The haters (Booker and that Ike) are the only ones, not believing in the Chiefs.  The believers are strong in their belief and feel that prayer has worked well for the Chiefs.  It certainly was not the coaching or the quarterback.  So after leaving early church on Sunday, look for the Chiefs to be 2-0, by three o’clock.  Believe, y’all.

paragraphs.text: Monday Niters
Be Careful And Cautious, With Those Chiefs

frames.text: Monday NitersBe Careful And Cautious, With Those Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Wow!  The New Orleans Saints are 2-0. So are seven other NFL teams.  One of them is the Kansas City Chiefs.
But, the Saints’ 2-0 is different than the Chiefs 2-0.
In our minds, the Saints will go on to capture the playoffs, if not repeat as World Champions. Whereas, our Chiefs. . . well, we ain’t sure just what will happen to them.

For those of us over 50, we have been down this road before.  Same stuff, a different year.  And the haters, among us, say it is about to end, this weekend at Arrowhead.  That’s when the Chiefs will face San Francisco, the same team that the Saints just beat this past Monday night.
Bottom line, most of us are basking in delight because we remember last year, when we were 0-2, at this time.

So, let’s all toast the Chiefs and their defense for making us “cautiously happy” with their play, thus far.  But, now let’s turn to the fella’s and see what they think about the Chiefs’ chances against the 49rs.

THE VENERABLE DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Doc is skeptical about the quarterback situation with the Chiefs.  He once bought a Cassel t-shirt but left it home and refused to wear it.  Look like he was right because the Chiefs could have won, without Cassel.
Doc says it was the defense, led by Derrick Johnson, that was the difference.  But. unlike the haters, Doc says the CHIEFS will win Sunday.

THE APOSTLE PA-UL BOOKER: He is the Executive Vice President of the Chiefs Haters.  And we don’t know where Paul started to go wrong. Many think he is overly influenced by another hater in the Monday Niters.
But, the saintly Paul says that SAN FRANCISCO will win on Sunday, ending the Chiefs good beginning.  He calls it the “Singletary Factor”, citing the 49rs’ head coach as the difference-maker.

THE COOL CARL CLARK: Like Doc, Carl is not impressed with Cassel, at all. However, he recognizes that both teams are better, this year, even though the Chiefs are weakly, overall.  Carl, not quite a hater, did select SAN FRANCISCO, to beat the Chiefs. At least by a field goal.  Maybe, Carl is being inducted into the Haters Hall Of Fame. ???
CONGRESSMAN EMANUEL CLEAVER: Steady on the campaign trail, it is fun to watch him take a break from Washington stuff.
In fact, he is slated to become Chairman of the Legislative Black Caucus in Washington, assuming he is re-elected.  That will give him even more access to the President and White House.
Go, Cleaver, go.

Obviously, he is doing fine representing Kansas City in Washington. But, the Congressman has allowed the haters to get to him.  He really believes the Chiefs will be “Gored” to death, citing the slashing running back from the Niners, Frank Gored.  Apparently, Ike and that Booker have gotten to Rev. . . he says SAN FRANCISCO BY 10.

FOREVER CANTA-NKEROUS IKE GARDNER: Last week, we observed Ike’s being nice to a certain group of employees at a local restaurant.  They secretly know I am right about his “porcupine-like” personality.  In fact, he has chosen to sit with only one other person, further distancing himself from his old friends.
To further this distance, Ike says that Haley and Cassel are “severe disabilities” and must be dealt with, some kinda way.  That leaves him no hope for the Chiefs this week. . .SAN FRANCISCO BY 13.

THE LOYALIST, LLOYD GREENFIELD: Lloyd tries to see hope in whatever he does. Being a part-time thespian, he can find positive, sometimes amid all hopelessness. And he needs it to for there are “haters” in this group.

However vocal the detractors are, Lloyd continues his support for the Chiefs. Specifically, he finds the running backs, Charles and Jones, as promising. Unlike the haters, Lloyd “gets it”. CHIEFS, all the way.

THE CNN OF KANSAS CITY, OLLIE HUBBARD: Now, Ollie believes that the Chiefs are going “up, up and away”.  Though he didn’t say where they were going, we assume he means the Chiefs will continue to win. However, we must remember that Ollie is a former hater and can’t be totally believed, right away.
When asked by how much, he proudly screams, CHIEFS BY 18.
Is he right?  Maybe, maybe not.
Now, back to CNN.
JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY: I have been friends with the Monday Niters for over forty years and this year, we will celebrate 40 years of uninterrupted friendship.
But, along the way, we have developed into a “two-party” system.  Some of us believe in the Chiefs, no matter what and there are those who DON’T believe in the Chiefs, no matter what.
As for me, the Chiefs will have to stop San Francisco’s Smith-to-Davis connection.  And with Kansas City’s weak secondary, one can see why we loyalists ought to be concerned.
In spite of this weakness, the return game and defense will be enough for the Chiefs to advance to 3-0. . .CHIEFS, ALL THE WAY.
EASY ED WEST: Ed is a computer geek.  In fact, he spent all of Monday night, player computer scrabble with his son, Damon (who is in California).  But Ed is perceptive, too.
He has seen the Arrowhead crowd make a difference and he is calling on their help to make the Chiefs an early contender.
But for Sunday, Ed has shifted over to the haters, after seeing San Francisco against the Super Bowl Champions Saints. SAN FRANCISCO BY A LOT.
Final Note: Too bad the Chiefs have let us down so many times before.  And unfortunately, we think of the Chiefs as losers, rather than victors.
But, whatever we do, we cannot allow these “tea-party like” haters predict and manage our future.
Clearly, the Chiefs are not New Orleans; but they are 2-0.  That makes them equal to the Saints and it is our perception of them that will dictate our expectations of them.

Dr. Allen, Lloyd, even Ollie, and I are aiming and expecting high.  While that Booker, Carl, Cleaver, Cantankerous Ike, and Ed West are usually right, the haters are not omnipotent and are wrong this time..
Let’s see, let’s see.

paragraphs.text: The Bible, literature, television and everyday life are full of examples of how the unexpected victor rises, in spite of the odds. Well, that theme is appropriate for the youthful Chiefs as they take on the long-respected Indianapolis Colts.  Yea, we know about the older, more war-like “Philistines”.  There’s Manning  and his passing partner, Reggie Wayne. And then on Kansas City’s side, there are the “Kids R Us”. And in “David and Goliath” fashion, these two teams will meet on Sunday, at noon, in Indianapolis.  And like David, the Chiefs only have a sling shot, and a bag of five stones to throw at last year’s AFC champion. Those five stones are Hali, McCluster, Johnson, Charles, and Jones.

It begs the question....can the Chiefs (fresh off a bye week) beat the Colts (fresh off a butt-kicking from Jacksonville)?  The answer is “yes they can”.  But, is it realistic? Yes! But, is likely? NO! And the Monday Niters line up just like those who predicted that Goliath would destroy the little kid, named David. Let’s look in and see what these “haters” think about Sunday’s game.

THE VENERABLE DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Doc is truly a bible reader.  He knows that the odds are against the Chiefs’ “kids”  But, he also knows that everyone thought that Goliath would destroy David.  Doc says repeatedly that the Chiefs are better than most people think.  Not a hater at all.  CHIEFS by 10.

THE APOSTLE PAUL BOOKER: Booker has consistently “hated on” the Chiefs.  And you can’t blame him for the Chiefs have been “shaky”, as all of us were when we were young. But, Booker says the “impossible” will never happen in Peyton’s Place.  Thus, he sees Goliath as the winner, on Sunday.  COLTS by 14

THE COOL CARL CLARK. . . Carl is not a hater and he is not a loyalist, either.  He’s on the fence a lot, often going with and against the Chiefs. Yet, he seems open to the possibility that the Chiefs may be a developing team that has not played a tough team yet. The Colts are that “tough” team. COLTS by 14

CONGRESSMAN “REV” CLEAVER: Definitely on the campaign trails these days, hoping to be re-elected to the United States Congress. In fact, he created a “preaching songbirds” program that will feature local ministers who sing to their congregations, as well as preach.  So forgive him if he fails to think clearly about the Chiefs and their new rise to prominence.  He’s been too busy campaigning and has allowed Ike and Booker to over-influence his thinking. He says the Chiefs are better, but not going to have a chance in Peyton Place. COLTS by 10.

IKE “PAW-PAW” GARDNER: A Chiefs “hater” from way back.  While intelligent, Ike just doesn’t see the light.  Without even thinking it through, he says the Chiefs are leading the NFL’s weakest division. He says the only way the Chiefs can win on Sunday is for the Colts to forfeit the game. Whew! He adds the Chiefs have too many “kids” on their 3-0 team. Regretfully he is taking GOLIATH AND THE COLTS by 17.

USUALLY LOYAL LLOYD GREENFIELD: Lloyd has been talk to Ikd and that Booker a lot lately, indicating that he is wavering in his belief about the Chiefs.  Usually, he is fearlessly backing the Chiefs.  But, like the Goliath crowd, he is changing his vote this time and going with the Colts. He believes the Chiefs “are still in their infancy” and cannot beat the Chiefs, at this time. COLTS by 6

OLLIE “CNN” HUBBARD: Any kind of news is Ollie’s business, whether true or untrue. And he thinks there will be “good news”, coming out of Indianapolis on Sunday.  As a member of Ebenezer AME Church, Ollie believes the Chiefs will sink a stone into the “forehead” of the Colts. A former hater, Ollie is now a believer/loyalist. CHIEFS by 3.

JIM “GRAND DAD” NUNNELLY:  Always supporting the youngsters.  He feels the Chiefs are re-tooled and have new skills, at every position i.e. running back, defensive line, linebackers, secondary, and even the offensive line and special teams. If there is a weakness, it is the “forced bye week” that came when the Chiefs were “rising fast”. Currently, the only undefeated team, the Chiefs will use their “rocks” wisely and overcome the “sluggish” Colts.  Face it yall, Goliath and the Colts are getting older and slower and showing signs of demise.  CHIEFS by 3.

ED “THE GEE” WEST: Ed is one of the few “senior citizens” who always packs his i-phone and laptop computer wherever he goes.  And he settles many an argument by just speaking into his phone.  His quiet demeanor serves him well for he usually goes with the facts and never allows the “haters” to get to him. Though he knows the Chiefs can throw running backs at the Colts all day Sunday.  And he knows that the Chiefs are vastly improved over years past.  But, he thinks the Chiefs don’t have enough to beat the Colts. COLTS all the way.

ERIC “ERICA’S DAD” WESSON: Eric has not drank the Chiefs’ kool aid yet. Yes they look good defensively in a lot of areas. He feels they have not been tested yet. San Diego is one dimensional  without their work horse running back LaDainian Tomlinson who they let go for some unknown reason. If I were the owner I would fire everyone who had something to do with that deal. Then they beat “no diminsional” Cleveland Browns and San Francisco. payton Manning in the man inspite of several losses early in the season. Once they start rolling they may win 12 games in a row including Sunday’s slacking of the Chiefs by 9.

Final Note: Everyone knows there is always a chance for the underdog.  Many of us have prevailed, when all the odds were totally not in our favor.  And that will be the motivation that the Chiefs will take into Indianapolis, Sunday.  Clearly, we are living in “changing times”.  Who would have thought we would ever have a black man in the White House?  And likewise, who would have thought the Chiefs would be undefeated and positioning themselves to become a contender? Those of you who line up with the “haters”, read First Samuel, Chapter 17, verse 49. Enough said.

paragraphs.text: You all will remember George Benson, a jazz singer-guitarist, who crooned his way into our memories with a song called, “Masquerade”.  The song was about a couple of lovers, who were “masking” their activities, which led to the question about a “masquerade”.
Well, the Chiefs are 4-2 now and many still think the Chiefs are not who we think they are. And this week will be a real test to see if the Chiefs are really “just masquerading”.  Hmmmm!
And like always, we Monday Niters are wondering if the Chiefs are really contenders for the playoffs or are they just “pretenders”.

First, they are us loyalists, who believe in the Chiefs, thick or thin, lose or win. We see hope in the making and like Obama used to say...yes, we can.  And then there are the “haters”, who despite some real evidence, still cling to the notion that the Chiefs will fade soon.  But, one “big hater” changed his vote this week. So, let’s inquire with each Monday Niter and query if the Chiefs will be playing beyond January 2.

Dr. Charles “The Chef” Allen:  Doc quit a good job at Bendix to pursue his life-long dream of becoming a dentist.  That he did and for thirty two years now, he has delivered “pain free” dentistry to this community.

So as the “main loyalist”, Doc sees the Chiefs undoubtedly making the playoffs. He finds great hope in the “B Boys”. He believes that Bowe and Berry are exactly what the “doc” ordered, on offense and defense respectively, No mask here. Chiefs by 10

Paul “Hater No. 1” Booker:  When Paul was an educator and a home-school coordinator for the District, he was kind, effective and knowledgeable.  Being from the Bootheel, he appeared that he was happy, go-lucky.  But, Paul was forced to pick cotton down in Haiti, Mo.  And he carries that “hate” with him, right onto things like the Chiefs.  No matter what the Chiefs do, Paul just says “no” to the Chiefs.  He says the same about their playoff chances. And about the Chiefs against winless Buffalo.  A real “hater”.  Take off your mask, Booker...it is a brand new day, Buffalo by 7.

Carl “Car Crazy” Clark: You want to see Carl light up?  Just ask him about his beloved, 1987 Corvette. He longs for that speed, that body, and that low center of gravity, But when asked about the Chiefs’ playoff chances, he is not as forward as Doc, nor as difficult as “that Booker”.  He recognizes some improvement but knows the Chiefs have not really been tested and have lost to the good teams, like Indianapolis and Houston.  So we might have to restore his Corvette to get him to say “yes” but for now, he is moving in the right direction. Chiefs by 3.

Congressman “Still Got It” Cleaver:  His wife, Dianne, took him to dinner, last Tuesday.  It was his birthday and despite a tedious campaign for re-election, he went and had fun. But the real fun will come on October 30 when the whole community is invited to help him celebrate his birthday, at Ararat Temple.

Evelyn Champagne King and the Bloodstones will be there to sing “happy birthday”, even though he is still wearing a mask about his real age.  But, on Sunday, he thinks the Chiefs will beat Buffalo and further enhance their chances of playing beyond the regular season.
Happy Birthday Rev and everyone will be there, with voter registration cards and five dollars. By the way, Ararat Temple is just north of the Peachtree Buffet. It all starts at 8. Chiefs by 10.

Ike “The Big Hater” Gardner:  Ike was once the chairman of the Desegregation Task Force, some 40 or so years ago.  And as an educator and a parent, he knew a lot about the “ins and outs” of the School District.  And when he is talking about that part of his life, he is kind, considerate and engaging.  However, he has grown to become a “hater of everything”.

Speak of the Chiefs and he will immediately inform you about the coaching “mental midgets”, referring to Haley and Weis. And this week, he has returned to his old, School District self.  He actually is predicting that the Chiefs, though still spotty, will beat Buffalo. POW! Did you get that, George Benson? Chiefs by 3

Lloyd “The Biker” Greenfield:   Lloyd owns a motorcycle. Not just any big bike.  It’s a Harley Davidson Soft Tail Heritage Motorcycle.  Now, that’s class. He once rode all the way to Houston, Texas on his toy, He still can be seen around town with his fellow Buffalo Soldiers, Peter Yelorda and Marques Harris.  While just cruising, Lloyd has often reflected on the Chiefs and how they have adopted some winning ways, slowly jelling into a playoff team.  There ain’t do doubt that the Chiefs will be going to the playoffs, starting Sunday out at Arrowhead.  Biking but betting on the locals. Chiefs by 6.

Ollie “Meet The Press” Hubbard:  Whenever you talk to Ollie, you feel like you are talking to the press.  You have to be real careful what you tell him because he is GONNA report it. But, all of us can attest to his helpful hospitality.  He will help you out, no matter what.  There ain’t no wearing a mask with Ollie.

He is who he is and we all accept and admire him for that.  In fact, Ollie has been the same, ever since he was a little boy, running in and out of his father’s barber shop, down on 18th Street.  That’s probably where his “inquiring mind” began.
But, Ollie knows that the Chiefs are back, just like he is with his ability to get around.  No doubt about it, Chiefs are contenders and he is going to tell everybody.  What’s new? Chiefs by 10.
Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly:  Came to town the same year the Chiefs qualified for the Super Bowl in 1969.

And after retiring from Jackson County, has returned to the health care industry, helping especially with Health Care Reform.  But, he remembers the glory days of the Chiefs.  Those like Otis Taylor and Buck Buchanan and Emmitt Thomas roamed our streets, patronized our businesses and attended our churches.

He yearns for the return to the good old days when the Rodgers Health center and Swope Health Services were born. There was no masquerading then for everyone had jobs and businesses were booming, up and down Troost and around 31st  street. That is when he met and became friends with all these Monday Niters.
He believes that the Chiefs are not “lost in a masquerade” and are rising again and will definitely make the playoffs. Chiefs by 22.

Ed “Mr. I-Phone” West: While the rest of us struggle with modern technology, Ed West welcomes it.  If a question about anything comes up, Ed just whispers into his i-phone and reads the answer.  Now, he does wish the i-phone had big print because he has to wear them triple-bi-focal glasses.  Nonetheless, he is a very valuable resource to our community.

Besides technology, Ed is actively engaged in helping teenagers adjust to the Raytown School District.  And while he is by far the most factual Monday Niter, he is by no means swayed by the invading “haters”.
He thinks the Chiefs are growing by “leaps and bounds” and will definitely win the AFC West. And he is not wearing a mask, at all.  Chiefs by 20.

But the real fun will come on October 30 when the whole community is invited to help him celebrate his birthday, at Ararat Temple.  Evelyn Champagne King and the Bloodstones will be there to sing “happy birthday”, even though he is still wearing a mask about his real age.  But, on Sunday, he thinks the Chiefs will beat Buffalo and further enhance their chances of playing beyond the regular season.Happy Birthday Rev and everyone will be there, with voter registration cards and five dollars. By the way, Ararat Temple is just north of the Peachtree Buffet. It all starts at 8. Chiefs by 10.Ike “The Big Hater” Gardner:  Ike was once the chairman of the Desegregation Task Force, some 40 or so years ago.  And as an educator and a parent, he knew a lot about the “ins and outs” of the School District.  And when he is talking about that part of his life, he is kind, considerate and engaging.  However, he has grown to become a “hater of everything”.  Speak of the Chiefs and he will immediately inform you about the coaching “mental midgets”, referring to Haley and Weis. And this week, he has returned to his old, School District self.  He actually is predicting that the Chiefs, though still spotty, will beat Buffalo. POW! Did you get that, George Benson? Chiefs by 3Lloyd “The Biker” Greenfield:   Lloyd owns a motorcycle. Not just any big bike.  It’s a Harley Davidson Soft Tail Heritage Motorcycle.  Now, that’s class. He once rode all the way to Houston, Texas on his toy, He still can be seen around town with his fellow Buffalo Soldiers, Peter Yelorda and Marques Harris.  While just cruising, Lloyd has often reflected on the Chiefs and how they have adopted some winning ways, slowly jelling into a playoff team.  There ain’t do doubt that the Chiefs will be going to the playoffs, starting Sunday out at Arrowhead.  Biking but betting on the locals. Chiefs by 6.  Ollie “Meet The Press” Hubbard:  Whenever you talk to Ollie, you feel like you are talking to the press.  You have to be real careful what you tell him because he is GONNA report it. But, all of us can attest to his helpful hospitality.  He will help you out, no matter what.  There ain’t no wearing a mask with Ollie.  He is who he is and we all accept and admire him for that.  In fact, Ollie has been the same, ever since he was a little boy, running in and out of his father’s barber shop, down on 18th Street.  That’s probably where his “inquiring mind” began.  But, Ollie knows that the Chiefs are back, just like he is with his ability to get around.  No doubt about it, Chiefs are contenders and he is going to tell everybody.  What’s new? Chiefs by 10.Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly:  Came to town the same year the Chiefs qualified for the Super Bowl in 1969.  And after retiring from Jackson County, has returned to the health care industry, helping especially with Health Care Reform.  But, he remembers the glory days of the Chiefs.  Those like Otis Taylor and Buck Buchanan and Emmitt Thomas roamed our streets, patronized our businesses and attended our churches.He yearns for the return to the good old days when the Rodgers Health center and Swope Health Services were born. There was no masquerading then for everyone had jobs and businesses were booming, up and down Troost and around 31st  street. That is when he met and became friends with all these Monday Niters.  He believes that the Chiefs are not “lost in a masquerade” and are rising again and will definitely make the playoffs. Chiefs by 22.Ed “Mr. I-Phone” West: While the rest of us struggle with modern technology, Ed West welcomes it.  If a question about anything comes up, Ed just whispers into his i-phone and reads the answer.  Now, he does wish the i-phone had big print because he has to wear them triple-bi-focal glasses.  Nonetheless, he is a very valuable resource to our community.  Besides technology, Ed is actively engaged in helping teenagers adjust to the Raytown School District.  And while he is by far the most factual Monday Niter, he is by no means swayed by the invading “haters”. He thinks the Chiefs are growing by “leaps and bounds” and will definitely win the AFC West. And he is not wearing a mask, at all.  Chiefs by 20.

paragraphs.text: The “F” Words

frames.text: The “F” Words

paragraphs.text: Carl Clark hosted the Monday Niters, this past week.  And amid the usual curses and smart comments, I asked the fellas to use “f” words, when giving their predictions and comments. It just seemed like something to do.  So what follows is a host of “f” words, sprinkled throughout the narrative.  See how many you can spot.

First off, the Chiefs are five and three, losing all three games on the road. But another fact is that they have won all three games and home plus one away game at Cleveland.  Most commentators, including our own, say the Chiefs are fading.  Well, that’s a bunch of flak.  Because this is the same team that everyone was raving fire about, just three weeks ago.  However discontented you may be, folk still believe the Chiefs are playoff-bound.

Losing to Oakland last week put them only a half game up on the Raiders.  And many say that San Diego is just beginning its usual, late-season rise.  But, don’t be moved by any of that crap. Chiefs still have fire-power and it will re-emerge against Denver on Sunday. If for no more than to save face.  Let’s now see what the guys say about the dreaded Denver game, in Denver.

Dr. Charles “A Real Likeable Guy” Allen: Doc believes that the Chiefs will commit a felony against the Broncos.  Quietly but forcefully, he says the Broncos don’t have a team that can match with the Chiefs. Practising pain-free dentistry for thirty two years, Doc says the Chiefs will still win the West.  Chiefs by 14

Paul “That Hater” Booker: Most people like Booker.  He’s pleasant and he’s a good road buddy.  There is no joint in town that Booker has not inspected. But, he’s a Chiefs hater, laughingly saying that the Chiefs fantasy time is over.  That Booker just can’t see the light, when it comes to the Chiefs.  He predicted rightly last week and that fact gives rise to his fight to end this Chiefs’ mania. He has sealed the Chiefs fate.  Denver by 3

Carl “Mr. President” Clark: You know Carl is now President of the Ivanhoe Club.  Along with folk like Jon Gray, he is trying to make life better for this century-old club.  After thinking it over for four weeks now, he thinks Carl has made a transition to a loyalist and he’s got the fever. Chiefs by 7

Congressman “Faith-filled” Cleaver: As you know, Cleaver just beat out a fakir, in his quest to retain his seat in Congress.  He actually sat down and chilled a little with us, this last Monday. He ate his little fish and followed up his comments with a funky remarked, aimed at Coach Haley.  Though he won’t forget that Oakland fiasco, he still believes in the Chiefs. Chiefs by 10

Ike  “Idi Amin” Gardner: I told yall about Ike’s aunt in Keytesville.  She is the only person Ike has ever feared.  While intellectually bright, he is obstinate and stubborn.  He will go to his final grave, hating the Chiefs.  But, he hates everything.  He will finagle the finest thing into something bad. So no use in trying to convert him into a loyalist.  He doesn’t forget and forever, remembers how many times the Chiefs’ coach has made a fantastic fool of himself.  One more reason to vote against the Chiefs. Denver by 7

Lloyd “A Gentlemen’s Gentleman” Greenfield: Lloyd filters out the facts, when thinking about his prediction.  Never quickly, he fills his mind with facts and filters out the crap. He knows that 5-3 is respectable for the Chiefs and we should never forget that. He believes the Chiefs are a work in progress and he advises all of us to file that away.  He says it will be fun, not fouls on Sunday. Chiefs by 6

Ollie “Elephant Memory” Hubbard: Everybody is amazed how Ollie remembers everything. He focuses in on everything so that he can repeat it later, sometimes at the worst times.  He flags his memory with everything for he is an ace reporter.  It is fair to say that Ollie is aware of the Denver-Chiefs feud, going back to the good old days. But without Shanahan, the Broncos are in their final stages, at 2-6.  That’s fair enough for Ollie. Chiefs by 10

Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: He faces everything squarely and will not forfeit his right to speak.  Like Ollie, that Cleaver and Ike accuse him of fonduing the truth. That makes him furious and lose control.  One of the most loyal people around, he thinks it is futile to entertain any more flak from haters. Anyway you look at it, the Chiefs are gonna make the playoffs.  So, stop the fussing and cussing....a sure thing for Sunday. Chiefs by 10

Ed “Clearheaded And Competent”  West: Ed is a little shell-shot. In fact, he fears the lack of fundamentals that pervade the Chiefs, at times.  He blames the recent loss to Oakland because McCluster wasn’t there.  But fast and furious, Dexter will return and fly up and down the field on Sunday...bring Ed to fulfill his desire to see the Chiefs elevate. Chiefs by 7

Eric “Amanda And Erica’s Dad” Wesson:  Frankly, I thought that the officiating in the Raiders win was a little fickled, especially the fumble call that led to the Chiefs’ final score. Bowe finally caught a pass and finished with a touchdown. But, I am glad that the Raiders won as I predicted with a field goal in the final drive and final second of the game in overtime. I think that he has caught at least one pass for a touchdown in the last four games. As far as the Broncos I think the Chiefs will finally get out of their funk and squeak by the Broncos by a final score of 13 to 14.  Chiefs by 1.

Final note:  The Chiefs are learning to play the game.  Winning means taking the bumps and bruises, as well as the roses and cheers.  And just think, we wrote this long article and never mentioned the most famous “F” word.  No need to use filth.  After all, it is all about the Chiefs. And we must stop talking about their funeral.  Ain’t gonna happen.

paragraphs.text: Ike Gardner is definitely one of a kind. We, in the Monday Niters, risk our emotional lives, each Monday night of the football season. That’s because Ike is cantankerous, arrogant, and one-wayward.
Of course, some of this “fearless candor” can be explained because Ike is/was an only child.

Spending most of his 79 years here, Ike is not a stranger at all. Best known as an educator/administrator, Ike was at the forefront of school desegregation issues, back in the early seventies. There, his candid ways saved the School District from courting catastrophe. He was not diplomatic at all...and thus, we still have some local conrol over our educational system.

In spite of this cantankerousness, Ike is well-respected in our football club. Dr. Allen and Ron Walton refer to him as a “friend for life”. Even though his rough-sounding baritone voice can be heard over everyone, he is well worth listening to.

Ike rants and rages his opinion, on anyone who will listen. Just this past Monday, Congressman Cleaver called Ike from Washington, just to check on his behavior. Ike talked Rev.’s head off, going on and on about the Chiefs. Rev actually hung up and Ike didn’t even notice. He just kept on “Ikeing” with fearless candor, leaving the rest of us speechless.

But, we must seriously consider what Ike says about the Chiefs and their Chiefs’ 5-0 start. Considering the weak schedule, Ike candidly warns us that there are still eleven games to play in 2013. And even though he is voting for the Chiefs to win against Oakland, he is nonetheless cautious about the Chiefs’ mediocrity. Oakland’s newly-found quarterback, Terrell Pryor, will test the Chiefs’ highly-rated defense. Listen to Ol’ Ike and his candor.
Enough of Uncle Cantank. . . now to the rest of us and our thoughts on the Chiefs and other things.

Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still reminding us about Alzheimer’s disease. Particularly, he advises care-givers that there is no cure for this awful, life-changing disease. However, he does see a great prognosis for the Chiefs and their momentum. . .Chiefs by 7
Paul Booker: He’s happy with the Chiefs’ progress and believes the defense will score often against the Raiders. . . Chiefs by 7
Carl Clark: Carl, on the other hand, believes the Chiefs are bound to lose, sometimes. And he thinks it will be Sunday, out at Arrowhead. Raiders by 7

Lloyd Greenfield: Everyone is commenting on Lloyd’s interest in total community education. Involving everyone in a child’s education is his strong view. Also, he is relentless about the Chiefs and the crowd. . . Chiefs by 3
Ollie Hubbard: Every now and then, Ollie gets out and about. And all the guys were elated to interact with him over dinner (that he didn’t cook or supervise). . . Chiefs by 7

Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly: He likes the Chiefs’ mental health. They are not breaking down, like they used to, last year. The Chiefs’ defense is among the leagues best, especially the front line and linebackers. Look for some errors but overall this is all. .. Chiefs by 10

Ed West:   Ed once managed the office of Citizens’ Complaints for the Police Department. Thus, he knows all about the need for local control. Leave it like it is, he shouts. Leadership is encouraging, even for the Chiefs. . . winning by 10

paragraphs.text: Aaron Alexis, Mental Health Conference, And The Chiefs

frames.text: Aaron Alexis, Mental Health Conference, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Just like always, our country is faced with another mental health dilemma, Someone kills up a lot a people and we turn our attention to the crime, and not the events leading up to the horror. Thank God, we are going to have a conference here in Kansas City that will address the entire issue of mental health and mental illness.

Yes, this Saturday at the Downtown Marriott, everyday folks will have an opportunity to talk about this woefully overlooked and under-discussed field. In fact, about 50 people from the urban core of Kansas City are signed up to participate in the day-long conversation. It’s all about planning and for once, we will be at the table, before it happens.
Now, what does this all have to do with the now-winning Chiefs.

Well, mental health controls everything we do. . . everything we think. . . and everything we try to do. And the Chiefs have been in a deep depression, for a long, long time. And now it appears that they are pulling themsellves out of it. That’s just what we all have to do. Address squarely the problem we are facing. The Chiefs went out and got a quarterback, some offensive linemen and a new coach. . . to address the losing streak and loss of fans.

And they are gaining the fans back, with their early efforts in the season. Dr. Charles Allen, Paul Booker, Bubba Cleaver, Lloyd Greenfield, Jim Nunnelly, and Ed West predicted that the Chiefs would win against Philadelphia. Of course, that cantankerous Ike Gardner and that garrulous Carl Clark thought the Chiefs have not changed, from last season.
But face it, the depression is lifting. The Chiefs are talking and looking better these days. They are working hard at addressing the things that hurt them. Just like we as individuals should do.
As we must do from time to time, we must remove cewrtain people from our lives. . .so that we can do better. In fact, the Chiefs are a lesson in regaining their mental health.

So, Dr. Allen will be going to the conference on Saturday to talk about Alzheimer’s season. Jim Nunnelly will be addressing the stigma, associated with people who are struggling mentally. And Andrea Buford will be facilitating discussion tables, down at the Marriott. It will all be part of a historical time where we in the urban community, will be talking about the future and not arguing about the past.
Maybe the first topic of discussion will be. . . how did the Chiefs overcome their depression.
The answer is simple and complex. It took a lot of time, patience, and a lot of support from people who used to love them.
All of you are invited to the Marriott on Saturday. Come see how to deal with mental health issues. With you becoming the focal point. . . for your own mental health.

paragraphs.text: The Hubbards, Opinions,
And The Chiefs

frames.text: The Hubbards, Opinions, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: The Monday Niters are full of themselves. They freely share their opinions and don’t care if  anyone agrees with them or not. And we’ll share some of those community-related opinions, right after we comment about the Hubbard family and their cooking talents.

This last Monday night was their time to host the Monday Niters. As usual, there was a feast. African cabbage, red beans and rice, chicken wings, catfish, spaghetti, green beans and potatoes, cole slaw, cornbread and rolls. Even their lovely daughter, Kim, dropped by to taste the Hubbard Buffet, But, there was something different tis week.

Usually, Ollie does all the cooking. But this time, it was his sassy wife, Sandra, who  did it all. Yes, Sandra. Now, she is no stranger to the culinary arts. Her late mother was truly a great cook. In fact, in Macon, Missouri, Mrs. McElroy was a well-known caterer throughout north central Missouri.

Now, if you don’t know where Macon is. It near Clarence, Missouri. Don’t know where that is. It’s near LaPlata, Still don’t know? Forget it. Neither do most people. But Sandra was the only black child in the school band. And she was the first black child born in the Macon County hospital. And she spent most of her days, living and thriving in an all-white world. But if you tasted her buffet on Monday, one would know she is truly an African American artist, when it comes to cooking.

Even Ike Gardner, the most opinionated African American alive, liked the red beans and rice. So did Ed West, who went back several times. But husband Ollie was present and offered his supervision to the whole process. Bottom line, the Hubbards did their thing, especially on Monday night. . . sharing their  cooking talents  and opinions.
Let’s start with Ollie and see what he and the other Monday Niters are thinking, about community events and the Chiefs.

Ollie Hubbard: Ollie is concerned about how all this violence is affecting our children. So, he is urging each of us to make sure our children stay in school for their own safety. But he is no longer concerned about the Chiefs. He says the Chiefs will kick the Giants’ butt, on Sunday. Chiefs by 10.

Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still concerned about Alzheimer’s disease. In fact, he says that the toll is not only on the patients but on the care-givers, as well. Caregivers often think the patient may get better and deny the reality of getting worse. But he thinks the Chiefs are “not in denial”. He says Sunday will be a “Giant killer day” for the 3-0 Chiefs. Chiefs by 14.

Paul Booker: He thinks the city leaders are on the right track, by inviting leaders from other cities to discuss the crime problem. Recent visitors from Chicago are helping us address this violence thing. He feels the same way about the Chiefs’ defense. They will slaughter Eli Manning on Sunday. Chiefs by 3.

Carl Clark: He believes that the sentencing ought to fit the crime. Bad crime, long time in jail. Just that simple. Feeling the same way about the Chiefs. They will be criminal, against New York. Giants by 14.

Emanuel “Bubba” Cleaver: Cleaver just finished his favorite week in Washington, hosting the Legislative Black Caucus. Only a few know how significant he is in Washington. Everybody knows and respects Emanuel Cleaver. And he knows the Chiefs will be like David and slaughter the Goliaths. Chiefs by 10.

Ike “Mad Man” Gardner: Ike is concerned about the lack of jobs. He feels that jobs are the crux of our social structure. Known for freely expressing his opinion. Ike is right about the jobs but wrong about the game on Sunday at Arrowhead. He thinks the Chiefs’ fairy tale is over. Giants by 7.

Lloyd Greenfield: He believes that to be educated is the key to a successful life. And that we must not let education get lost in all the violence discussions. Like with the Chiefs, we must “keep on keeping on”. Chiefs by 3.

Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly: He is still reeling over the central city representation at the recent Mental Health speak-out. One-third of the participants were African American and they came through like champs, offering their insightful opinions freely. Congratulations to each of you that attended. Now, let’s not allow the Chiefs to get depressed again. Jamaal Charles and the defense will stop that from happening. Chiefs by 7

Ed West: He still harping on the police control thing. Plainly, the control of the police department should be left alone. Period. And look to the Chiefs defense (Poe, Hali and Houston)  to shut Eli down. Chiefs by 10.

paragraphs.text: Ed West is by far the most knowledgeable and most practical Monday Niter. Between naps, he always lends facts to our highly opinionated discussions. All he does is pull out his Iphone and recites the facts.

And that technological move silences the voices of those who are just talking to hear themselves talk. Ed learned about computers at an early age. He was a manager at the old Western Electric Plant, out in Lee’s Summit.

Further, Ed was once the executive in charge of Citizens’ Complaints of the Police department. His knowledge about technology, coupled with his commitment to listening to citizens is a major reason for his widespread, community support. He is respected, admired and often called on to address personal computer issues among his friends.

In addition, his Monday Niter friends agree with him when he says the Chiefs are just as good as Denver. In fact, he pulled out his computer and concluded that except for Baltimore, the Chiefs and Denver have played the same teams. However, he does concede that Denver has beaten their opponents by wider margins. Bottom line.....six victories is six victories...no matter who the team is. But let’s look in on the proceedings from a great Monday night, with the Monday Niters. Here’s some highlights of the long discusions:

Dr. Allen is still persistent about Alzheimer’s and caregivers. In fact, he thinks this research tax must include something about care-givers. More on this next week. . . Congressman Cleaver calls Booker from Washington, just to check on him....Jim Randall, Booker’s neighbor, drops in. . . Ike, Dr. Allen and Booker talk about their days at Niles Home. . . Ed West nods. . .Why aren’t the Chiefs throwing to Dwayne Bowe?. . . Chiefs cannot beat Denver, period. . . Josh Freeman of Grandview will eventually become the starting quarterback for Minnesota. . . Ed is snoring loudly now. . . The Chiefs are running Jamaal Charles to death. . . San Diego always folds down the line. . . remember it was the Baltimore Ravens who beat Denver last year and won the Super Bowl. . . the way the Republicans are acting is paving the way for Hillary Clinton to be President..Carl and Lloyd talk about how many of their classmates have died. . . Cleaver says that “it is crazy up here in Washington”. . .but he’s hanging in there. . .Dontari Poe is doing his thing as the Chiefs’ nose tackle. . . Chiefs lead the league in defense. . . so what will the Chiefs do against the Houston Texans, out at Arrowhead on Sunday?
Dr. Charles Allen: KC is in the easy part of their schedule. Chiefs by 14.
Paul Booker: KC has a better defense. Chiefs by 7.
Carl Clark: KC is weak on offense. Houston by 3.
Ike Gardner: Same plague that struck the Giants struck Houson. Chiefs by 7.
Lloyd Greenfield: KC’s offense will step up Sunday. Chiefs by 3.
Ollie Hubbard: Lincoln University could beat these Texas cowboys. Chiefs by 7.
Jim Nunnelly: KC has All-Pro Defense. No losses until Dennver.Chiefs by 17.
Ed “Awake Now” West: KC has superior defense and a great crowd.Chiefs by 10.
Walt Youngblood: It’ll be a defensive struggle Chiefs by 3.Jim Randall: Homefield advantage Chiefs by 14
Clancy Parker: .Following Doc Allen. Chiefs by 7.

paragraphs.text: Mila Banks threw her own 100th birthday party, over at the Marriott at 45th and Main last Sunday. About 400  former students, fellow educators, and Christian friends stood in line to congratulate such a remarkable woman.

And at the dinner party, we, Monday Niters and wives attended and, were represented by cantankerous Ike Gardner. It was Ike’s idea to make “Ms.  Banks” an honorary Monday Niter. That’s because she is a loyal reader and a good friend to so many of us.
So, Ike presented her with a trophy and told that crowd that she will be making her Chiefs’ predictions, right along side ours.
But last Monday night  Gen Greenfield prepared a dinner of fresh sweet potatoes and freshly fried fish and a phenomenal salad. Who could argue about anything, with a meal like that in front of you?

So the Monday Niters, along with the Go-Along group spent the entire night, talking about how African Americans have been failed by various educational ploys. Here is how some of the conversation went. After that, we will give our predictions on the Buffalo-Chiefs game, coming up Sunday in Buffalo. Ms. Banks will make her prediction, as well. Here goes:
There was a time in Kansas City’s history when students coming from the Deep South were routinely put back a grade.

Also, during segregation days, black children from Independence, Excelsior Springs and Pleasant Hill were bussed into the Kansas City Mo., School District. Well into the sixties, there were still one-room schools in the state of  Georgia.

In the Bootheel of Southeast Missouri, black students were bussed up to 60 miles each day to attend school. Because cotton was “king”, black kids went to school in “split sessions” i.e. their school year was interrupted to allow for the picking and chopping of cotton.
Ms. Banks attended school in Mount Vernon, about 46 miles west of Springfield, Mo. Because of its erudite faculty, Lincoln High school was rated highly nationwide.
Earning college credit while in high school is not a new thing. This was done in the sixties through such great educators like Jeremiah Cameron, Neal Herrford and Chester Anderson.

Dr. Charles Allen attended Sumner Elementary and Ike, Carl and Lloyd attended, Wendell Phillips way back in the thirties and forties. Ed West attended school in Osawatomie, Kansas and Jim Nunnelly attended segregated schools in Columbia, Mo.
Ms. Banks received unexpected help with her tuition to Lincoln university, way back in the thirties.

Today, educating black kids is still an issue in Kansas City.Students who want to leave the unaccredited Kansas City, Mo., School District to attend a nearby accredited school district, are met with the problem of who is to pay for all of this.....the more things change, the more they stay the same.
Not so for the Chiefs....they will be 9-0 at the end of the day, Sunday. Here are our thoughts about the Chiefs:
Mila  Lewis Banks: Chiefs by 10
Dr. Charles Allen: Chiefs by 10
Paul Booker: Chiefs by 3
Carl Clark: Buffalo by 3
Bubba Cleaver: Chiefs by 7
Ike Gardner: Buffalo by 3
Lloyd Greenfield: Chiefs by 7
Ollie Hubbard: Chiefs by 10
Jim  “GrandDad”  Nunnelly: Chiefs by 2
Ed West: Chiefs by 10
Joe Webster: Chiefs by 6
Rick Davis: Chiefs by 10
Willie Humphrey: Chiefs by 7
Paul Knight: Chiefs by 11
Marshall Robinson: Chiefs by 9
Mike McNeil: Chiefs by 12
Sander Martin: Chiefs by 14

paragraphs.text: Stewart Watson was a big, giant of a guy, who always wore a smile and had a baritone-like laugh. He was “at home” whereever he went, whether in his favorite club on Prospect or whether meeting you for the first time. He clearly will be missed by all of us Monday Niters for he was one of the founding members of this adult “boys club”.
To most of us, he had  been friends for all of his 24,582 days on this earth. But on July 3, of this year, “Bunny Rabbit” left this earth and thus, the basic reason for this column.
In short, we want to say “good bye” in a way that only friends who have known you a lifetime, can say it. So let’s start with “Bunny Rabbit” and his relentless use of nicknames.

“Bunny Rabbit” had a nickname for everyone in our group. That’s because he wanted each of us to know that he liked each of us individually and collectively. Ollie was “Mr. Puddy Pot”  and Ike was “Huff”. Booker was “Chocolate Drop”. Dr. Allen was “Pumpkin” and Carl was appropriately called “Mr. Mary Lynn”. And because of my bald head, he started calling me “Mr. Peanut”. I dare say he would have to stop and think of our real names because that was all he called us, every day of his nearly 69 years.  We say nearly because he died just three days before his 69th birthday. And there was no denying him access to you. Even though he moved to St. Louis some years ago, he still managed to see everyone at least once a month or just calling them.

Speaking of calling, “Bunny Rabbit” was a phone junkie.  Night or day, winter or fall, he would call one of us, out of the clear blue sky. It was as if we were his connection to reality or maybe he just wanted to stay close to his friends. Always the same, joy-induced greeting, “ what u doing boy?”. And then, right from there, the word would spread... “Bunny Rabbit” is in town and somehow, unplanned though it may be, there would be a reunion, right then and there. And it seemed he would always time his visit during one of our Monday Nite Footballers meeting and whatever the conversation on the floor, would give way to his one-man, nickname-calling comedy act.  “Bunny Rabbit” was a real friend and the kind of brother to everyone, even though he had no biological brothers or sisters. He exuded brotherhood, at its highest level.

In addition, “Bunny Rabbit” was a  lesson in kindness and consideration. He reminded us that we all must live our lives, merrily and among friends.  He demonstrated that by always dropping by and diverting you from your daily worries and strife. Yes, Bunny Rabbit was a spark of life to all of us and his light still shines in our thoughts and in our conversation. Ike says “Bunny Rabbit” always checked on him whether sick or well. And Ollie says that he has great memories of “Bunny” all the way from elementary school through Lincoln university.
But, Dr. Charles Allen concluded the stories about “Bunny Rabbit” best.

He simply said that “Bunny Rabbit” extended a hand but he always touched our hearts. What else needs to be said but “Good Bye, ‘Bunny Rabbit’. We are all better off by knowing you and we will wear our nicknames proudly, in your honor.”

paragraphs.text: John Legend, Paul Booker And The 9-0 Chiefs

frames.text: John Legend, Paul Booker And The 9-0 Chiefs

paragraphs.text: John Legend wrote and dedicated a song to his recent bride. In that song, he just pours out his heart, telling her that “all of me loves all of you….your edges, your curves, and your perfect imperfections”. John Legend is saying that he realizes her love has some shortcomings, but he loves her deeply just the same.

Now that’s just what most of us feel about our Chiefs. They have a perfect record but most of us are willing to live with their “perfect imperfections”. Some people even say the Chiefs are a fluke and are just waiting for them to show how imperfect they really are. But Paul Booker isn’t one of them. He’s been voting for the Chiefs all year long, despite voting against them all last year.

But Paul is more supportive this year. Always a Chiefs’ supporter ever since he came to town, way back in 1966. A veteran of the Air Force and a graduate of Lincoln university, Paul is a very likeable educator, having taught at Woodland, Switzer, Southeast Middle, Greenwood and C.A. Franklin schools. And he is generally healthy and is recovering graciously from the loss of his wife a few months ago. So these days, he is just trying to “maintain” and keep going. So the Chiefs are giving him the “perfect boost” that he needs.

Paul knows the Chiefs lack a consistent offense, even though the defensive unit is actually carrying the team. In spite of that, Paul expects the Chiefs to beat Denver on Sunday night. Yes, along with Ed West, Greenfield, Dr. Allen, Mrs. Banks and Ollie, Paul  is predicting a long-shot victory over the Manning-led Broncos. But his former boss, Ike Gardner and his 6902 buddy, Carl Clark, believes the Chiefs will succumb and lose, out in the mile-high city Paul and the other Chiefs supporters are thinking 10-0 and a sure-shot for the playoffs and maybe even the Western Division championship.
But, not so fast. Ike and Carl are quick to point out the Chiefs’ imperfections. They say Manning will get rushed, even sacked a couple of times..but he will burn the “imperfect” secondary all night.

Conversely, both Booker and Cleaver remember the 100 yard interception return by Sean Smith and say proudly that the “perfect defense” will more than make up for any flaws in the Chiefs’ secondary. In fact, they say that “special D” has held all opponents to less than seventeen points, throughout all nine games.

All in all, all of us love all of the Chiefs. And we know it will be something to behold, if the Chiefs win it all. And if they don’t, we will still support them, in spite of their “imperfectness”. The Denver Broncos will be playing hard because they didn’t expect such an upsurge from the Chiefs. So, all eyes will be on the Chiefs, this Sunday night. National television. Suspect commentators. Possible championships. And like John Legend, we hope that those edges and imperfections don’t show up. At least, not Sunday night:
Dr. Charles Allen: says “why change? The Chiefs are winning” Chiefs by 10
Mrs. Mila Banks:   It’s going to be a tight game, without a doubt. Chiefs by 3
Paul Booker:    Chiefs will crank up the “imperfect” offense. Chiefs by 13
Carl Clark:  I’ve been predicting against the Chiefs all year. Denver by 10
Bubba Cleaver: Chiefs won’t be out-MANNINGED. Chiefs by 3
Ike Gardner:  The Chiefs’ perfect bubble will burst. Denver by 17
Lloyd Greenfield:  Defense will come alive, no jive. Chiefs by 7
Ollie Hubbard:   Chiefs will keep it going. Chiefs by 7
Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: John Legend and Lisa Washington know about perfection.                              Chiefs by 1
Ed West:   Chiefs have performed well enough to win and the defense will get to “Perfect Peyton”.   Chiefs by 3

John Legend is saying that he realizes her love has some shortcomings, but he loves her deeply just the same.Now that’s just what most of us feel about our Chiefs. They have a perfect record but most of us are willing to live with their “perfect imperfections”. Some people even say the Chiefs are a fluke and are just waiting for them to show how imperfect they really are. But Paul Booker isn’t one of them. He’s been voting for the Chiefs all year long, despite voting against them all last year. But Paul is more supportive this year. Always a Chiefs’ supporter ever since he came to town, way back in 1966. A veteran of the Air Force and a graduate of Lincoln university, Paul is a very likeable educator, having taught at Woodland, Switzer, Southeast Middle, Greenwood and C.A. Franklin schools. And he is generally healthy and is recovering graciously from the loss of his wife a few months ago. So these days, he is just trying to “maintain” and keep going. So the Chiefs are giving him the “perfect boost” that he needs. Paul knows the Chiefs lack a consistent offense, even though the defensive unit is actually carrying the team. In spite of that, Paul expects the Chiefs to beat Denver on Sunday night. Yes, along with Ed West, Greenfield, Dr. Allen, Mrs. Banks and Ollie, Paul  is predicting a long-shot victory over the Manning-led Broncos. But his former boss, Ike Gardner and his 6902 buddy, Carl Clark, believes the Chiefs will succumb and lose, out in the mile-high city Paul and the other Chiefs supporters are thinking 10-0 and a sure-shot for the playoffs and maybe even the Western Division championship.But, not so fast. Ike and Carl are quick to point out the Chiefs’ imperfections. They say Manning will get rushed, even sacked a couple of times..but he will burn the “imperfect” secondary all night. Conversely, both Booker and Cleaver remember the 100 yard interception return by Sean Smith and say proudly that the “perfect defense” will more than make up for any flaws in the Chiefs’ secondary. In fact, they say that “special D” has held all opponents to less than seventeen points, throughout all nine games. All in all, all of us love all of the Chiefs. And we know it will be something to behold, if the Chiefs win it all. And if they don’t, we will still support them, in spite of their “imperfectness”. The Denver Broncos will be playing hard because they didn’t expect such an upsurge from the Chiefs. So, all eyes will be on the Chiefs, this Sunday night. National television. Suspect commentators. Possible championships. And like John Legend, we hope that those edges and imperfections don’t show up. At least, not Sunday night:Dr. Charles Allen: says “why change? Chiefs by 13Carl Clark:  I’ve been predicting against the Chiefs all year. Denver by 10Bubba Cleaver: Chiefs won’t be out-MANNINGED. Chiefs by 3Ike Gardner:  The Chiefs’ perfect bubble will burst. Denver by 17Lloyd Greenfield:  Defense will come alive, no jive. Chiefs by 7Ollie Hubbard:   Chiefs will keep it going. Chiefs by 7Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: John Legend and Lisa Washington know about perfection.                              Chiefs by 1Ed West:   Chiefs have performed well enough to win and the defense will get to “Perfect Peyton”.   Chiefs by 3

paragraphs.text: Long before Kerry Washington became “a Thursday night must-see”, she starred along side Jamie Foxx in the 2004 major flick, “Ray”.

In fact, she played Ray Charles’ wife and stood firm and steady, all through Ray Charles’ ups and downs and yes, even a nasty heroin addiction. We all knew then that Kerry would rise to the top, especially since she possesses the ability to use “all of her” in her acting craft. Eyes. Nose, Forehead. Eyebrows.Facial creases. This woman exudes totality and entirety. Everything about her makes the scene advance. When acting, Kerry rules.

Speaking of rules, let’s talk a minute about the Golden Rule. While many think this is a biblical expression, it really came along, long before Christianity. It simply says “do unto others as you would have them do unto you”. Well, the Chiefs will have a chance to do just that against Denver this Sunday. Beaten badly in the “mile-high” city two weeks ago, the Broncos will come riding into Arrowhead, after a horse-whipping from the New England Patriots last Sunday. Yes, Denver jumped out to a 24-0 lead, only to fall to the “totally magic arm” of Tom Brady. Eventually, the Patriots prevailed with a record-breaking comeback, in the second half. The first half, all Denver. The second half, it was all New England.
That brings us to the Chiefs and Denver. Both teams are vying for the AFC West and a guarantee of home-field advantage in the playoffs. And really, it’s much more.

Kansas City has to prove that it can “hang” with the best teams, a second time. Against San Diego, the offense finally showed up and the defense went to sleep. Jamaal Charles ran like crazy, while Hali and Houston fell to injuries.
And more important, “AWOL Alex” Smith threw for nearly 300 yards. Where in the hell have you been, Alex?
Bottom line, the Chiefs will need everything and everybody to beat Denver, especially since Denver was” totally embarrassed” before God and country.
Like Kerry Washington, the Chiefs will need to express themselves, just like Smith finally did.

Otherwise, the Kansas City fans will consider it a “scandal” and turn the tv off, reminding us of the days-gone-by when they lost all the time. Ahhhh. An idea. Let’s call in Olivia Pope and see if she can fix this scandal or do something to make it right.

No, not just yet. Let’s give the Chiefs one more chance, to put together a complete game, where the offense moves the ball and the defense rides the bucking Broncos. Faith. Faith. Faith. Just a little more faith. And a lot of the Golden Rule.
Dr. Charles Allen: It’s a “must-win”.            Chiefs by 10.
Mrs. Mila Lewis Banks:  Chiefs lost their best tacklers. Denver by 7.
Paul Booker:   K.C’s defense is no longer enthusiastic. Denver by 14
Carl Clark: Alex Smith has been exposed.  Denver by 7.
Bubba Cleaver: These are troubling times in the kingdom. Denver by 10.
Ike Gardner: Defense is nonexistent without Hali and Houston. Denver by 20.
Lloyd Greenfield: It’ll be a struggle, but K.C. will prevail.      Chiefs by 3.
Ollie Hubbard:  Do unto others as they HAVE done unto you.         Chiefs by 6.
Jim Nunnelly:  K.C. will employ Kerry-Washington-like totality.   Chiefs by 6.
Ed West: KC has too many defensive injuries. Denver by 10.

paragraphs.text: It is Christmas time and we are all singing those long-remembered Christmas carols. One song stands out, as the Chiefs enter the much-coveted playoff/Super Bowl pursuit. Y’all know the story about Rudolph. He had this freaky red nose and the other reindeer “used to laugh and call him names”. They never let Rudolph join in any reindeer games. Okay, you get the point. But, one foggy Christmas eve, ol’ Rudolph became the MVP among reindeers, everywhere.

Speaking of Most Valuable Player, we must begin to talk about “who is the Chiefs’ MVP this year”. Dr. Allen says it will be indisputably Jamaal Charles. Even wishy-washy Paul Booker says Charles is an all-purpose player and deserves to be MVP. Mr. Socialite, Carl Clark, adds that Charles is “the team”. And Mila Banks closes the conversation by saying that Charles is “running well and scoring”.
That sums it all up….Jamaal Charles is the MVP of the 2013 Chiefs. Please note that Ike Gardner was not asked about his opinion on this.

That was on purpose. Because Ike’s approval rating has sunk to an all-time low. Most people at St. James forgive Ike for his cantankerous ways. Sometimes, he is just against everything, You will remember it was Ike who said the Chiefs would only win four games this year. And even in spite of winning eleven games already, he insists on saying the Chiefs will lose this Sunday, out at Arrowhead.

This abject stubbornness caused Mila Banks to lash out at old Ike. She says that Ike needs to wake up and “know that the Kansas City is playing football”. Meaning, Ike you can stop berating the Chiefs because they have proved your tired self wrong.

In  fact, many say that the book “A Christmas Carol” was written about Ike Gardner. It has been said that Ebenezer Scrooge and Ike were room-mates, at one time. Unfortunately, Ike still corresponds with Scrooge frequently. They talk about everything, including how Santa still is using reindeer to deliver Christmas packages..

Speaking of reindeer, let’s return to close out the thought about “Rudolph”. He was ostracized just like the Chiefs were last year. People laughed and talked badly about Rudolph. Like the Chiefs, everyone said ol’ Rudolph was a loser and would never amount to nothing. And now, this year, everyone is acting like they never said anything bad about the Chiefs. Those same haters are rushing home from church, talking about how proud they are of their hometown team.

Bottom line, it was Ike who stirred up the other reindeer against Rudolph, in the first place. So the next time you see Ike Gardner, tell him that Rudolph and the Chiefs are now on top. And like Mila Banks said to Ike…”wake up and know” that even Scrooge changed when presented with facts. Not so with that damn Ike. He has fallen asleep again.
Dr. Charles Allen: K.C.’s offense will destroy. Chiefs by 7
Mila Banks: K.C. is playing football. Chiefs by 10
Paul Booker: K.C. has developed a winning spirit. Chiefs by 3
Carl Clark: K.C.’s defense is not ready for Indy. Colts by 10
Bubba Cleaver: K.C. will “harsh collar” the Colts. Chiefs by 7
Ebenezer Gardner: the Colts will leave their horseshoe prints on the Chiefs’ behind. Colts by 7
Lloyd Greenfield: I believe. Chiefs by 7
Ollie Hubbard: K.C. will catch Indy “napping”. Chiefs by 6
Jim Nunnelly: Charles earns his MVP stripes. Chiefs by 10
Ed West: Full team effort and home field.Chiefs by 3

paragraphs.text: Interim Superintendent
And The Lowly Chiefs

frames.text: Interim Superintendent And The Lowly Chiefs

paragraphs.text: The NFL season is finally here. After a threatened strike, a boatload of free agents, and a new set of feet, the Chiefs will open at Arrowhead on Sunday. And you will see folks going to early morning church services, in order to witness the kickoff game to the 2011 season. And like the tornado that hit Joplin and the hurricane Irene that racked the east coast, the Chiefs have a lot of damage to clean up. You know they released All Pro offensive lineman, Brian Waters. And Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel is ailing, as usual. Then, the Chiefs did not win a single pre-season game, this summer. That all adds up to another questionable season ahead, in spite of the fact the Chiefs made the playoffs last year.

In many ways, the Chiefs are like the Kansas City, Mo., School District.  Every year, they come up with a different reason why any kind of success evades them. In fact, Big Bad John Covington balanced the budget but he did absolutely nothing to improve the test scores. He closed a lot of schools but did not open up any new academic trails.  And once again, Booker says it is purely chaotic, down at 1211 McGee. No one knows what to do about it and that’s tragic. As expected each year, the enrollment, the energy and the ebullience decreases.

I suggest that at least the Board ought to hire an Associate Superintendent, whose only job is to monitor the academic progress of our children and keep the community updated on the accreditation status.  This person should be a resident of Kansas City and  have credibility in our community.  This over-reliance on itinerant Superintendents is crazy. And we in this community can change that. We really can. All right, enough of that.  Let’s return to talking about the Cheaps (I mean Chiefs).

Ike Gardner and Paul Booker are back at their old habits again. They can’t see the Chiefs beating anybody this year. After all, the Chiefs play New England, San Diego twice, Pittsburg, Minnesota, Indianapolis, and even Detroit. That’s what happens when a non-playoff-calibre teams make the playoffs, They suffer greatly the next year. But Carl Clark, Ollie Hubbard, and of course, Dr. Charles Allen believe the Chiefs will be “up” for the challenge and will win their first game, against Buffalo. So, like the School District, the Chiefs are steadily losing their support....both here and nationally.
What will it take to get it back for both of these also-rans?

It’s simple. Just do SOMETHING right. Anything. Is help on the way? As is our duty, we will monitor the progress and report to you each week.  Just like we have been doing for forty two years now. Whew! Time passes, doesn’t it.  Hint to the District and the Chiefs.
