paragraphs.text: African Cabbage, Mrs. Myla Banks, And The Chiefs

frames.text: African Cabbage, Mrs. Myla Banks, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: We, Monday Niters, know that when we go to Dr. Allen’s house, there will be “something new”. Of course, Dr. Allen, a long-respected dentist, fashions himself as a culinary artist. He thrives on finding different foods to serve us.

This week it was African cabbage, merlot-induced gravy, a medley of beans, macaroni with ham and peas, fried chicken strips and Yorkshire pig feet. Yes, we had pig feet and it was presented as a delightful delicacy.
Of course, Dr. Allen recognized the essential contributions of his daughter, Tee and his wife, Beverly. Commonly called the “A Team”, they helped us celebrate the Chiefs’ victory over Green Bay.
It certainly helped that Dr. Allen was the only Monday Niter to pick the Chiefs over Green Bay. So he was all smiles. Even overly-mean Ike Gardner was grinning.

That’s because Mrs. Myla Banks, a long-time educator in the Kansas City Missouri School District, actually phoned Ike. That shows you how nice Mrs. Banks is because no one calls Ike just to chat. Right there in the middle of the game, he and Mrs. Banks talked about old times and she chided Ike for being so hard on the Chiefs. In fact, she flat-out told him she was picking the Chiefs over Oakland, Saturday at Arrowhead. Of course, everyone saluted Mrs. Banks because she has been one of our most faithful readers of our column. That’s a blessing because Mrs. Banks still can be seen around town, talking to the owner of the Chiefs or conversing at the annual NAACP luncheon.
Thanks, Mrs. Banks, but that wasn’t all that happened.

Paul “Hater of All Haters” Booker actually made a confession, stopping all the usual noise. And you will have to read his comments below to find out exactly what he said to “blow us all away”. We were floored and most of us went home, knowing that Booker had been “touched” by something. The 19-14 victory over Green Bay must have surprised him big-time. And so it was with the Chiefs.

The Chiefs could not believe it, themselves. Green Bay came to town, undefeated and expected to just beat up the lowly-Chiefs and move on toward the Super Bowl. But, Tambi Hali and the defense gave the offense some room. And the new quarterback, Orton, looked like he “done found him a job”. When was the last time you saw a Chiefs’ quarterback zip a pass between two defenders? Face it, Orton is the “O” factor and should be expected to help the Chiefs this week. And if things work out against Oakland, then the new Chiefs with the “O’ factor will return to Denver, against the team that cut him four weeks ago. Speaking of Oakland, will the Chiefs make a serious run for the playoffs? Let’s see what the Monday Niters think. Now, be sure to look for what Booker said.

Dr. Charles Allen: The new coach, Romeo Crennel, has created a new culture in the Chiefs’ organization. That culture led to a big, unexpected showing against Green Bay. The formidable Packers were not looking for a tough game against the Chiefs. But the Chiefs came through, just like Charles said they would. Chiefs by 10
Paul “the Converted Apostle” Booker: Booker says the change in attitude among the players is remarkable. They just wouldn’t play for Todd the Tyrant.
Like Patti LaBelle, the Chiefs now have a “new attitude”. And because of that, Booker is picking the Chiefs over Oakland.
Do you believe it?
He is parting waves with “that” Ike and  has accepted the Chiefs as winners. Praise the Lord. Chiefs by 7

Carl Clark: Carl still thinks the Chiefs were lucky last Sunday, against Green Bay. Even though the Chiefs controlled the ball longer, sacked Aaron Rodgers several times, and even scored on two long drives.
Still, Carl is not convinced and he has now taken on Booker’s old role, as a “hater”.  Oakland by 7

Congressman Cleaver: Cleaver is still in Washington, trying to get the Republicans to pass a tax-cut bill for the middle class. In fact, they are about to make “Rev.” mad. That’s because Rev. wants all of us to pay less payroll taxes and the Republicans are holding it up. And it is driving Rev insane with this kind of duplicity. Anyway, Rev is convinced the Chiefs played well and will probably do the same against the Raiders. . . so. . . Chiefs by 7

Ike “Oldest Grench Alive” Gardner: Ike enjoyed talking to Mrs. Myla Banks. He even smiled a time or two, during the ten-minute conversation. That made him say later that he was glad that dumb-ass Haley was no longer coaching the Chiefs. And he kind of sighed when he learned that his long-time-hater-ally,  Booker had been converted to the Chiefs. That made him mad and he again denounced the Chiefs. . .what’s new?. . .Oakland by 10

Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd says that Green Bay just under-estimated the Chiefs. It is refreshing to see the Chiefs playing as a team. They have recovered quickly from “Haley-itis”, which led them to mess up and not score. Lloyd is cautiously optimistic about the Chiefs winning the next two games. . .but starting Saturday. . . it is the. . . Chiefs by 3

Ollie “Dr. Death” Hubbard: Just the other day, Applejack Matthews commented that Ollie is among the world’s most informed obituary experts. And Ollie is not yet sounding the death alarm for the Chiefs. He thinks that this is just the beginning of a “new day” for the Chiefs. He is sending a loud message to his cousin, Faye, in Oakland. Chiefs by 5

Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: There was a song by the Persuaders, called “ A Thin Line Between Love And Hate”. That’s how I feel about the Chiefs...you like ‘em one minute and hate ‘em the next. But last Sunday, no one hated the Chiefs. People everywhere were praising them, just like the were the new “David”, slaying Goliath Green Bay. More important, Romeo Crennel looks like he “done found a job too”. But he gotta win Christmas Eve against Oakland and New Year’s Day out at Denver. . . he will, at least this Saturday at Arrowhead. Chiefs by 6

Ed “Always Right” West: Ed never got over hiring a golf coach to coach pro football. You will remember Haley was a golf coach at one time and Ed has never supported him. But Ed is quick to praise Crennell for his philosophy includes both the offense and defense. Coming from a real football player, Ed is again right, especially about Romeo’s Christmas gift to the fans. Chiefs by 7

Eric “Last Second Christmas Shopper” Wesson: It is just hard to gauge what the Chiefs are going to do. They play so inconsistent. They allow Miami, which had not one any games, come in and beat them soundly. Then they send Green Bay packing in a game they really had no chance, on paper, of winning. But, I suppose a quarterback and coach will make a difference.
The Chiefs, will beat the Raiders by 10. Get Romeo’s three-year contract ready.

The 19-14 victory over Green Bay must have surprised him big-time. And so it was with the Chiefs.The Chiefs could not believe it, themselves. Green Bay came to town, undefeated and expected to just beat up the lowly-Chiefs and move on toward the Super Bowl. But, Tambi Hali and the defense gave the offense some room. And the new quarterback, Orton, looked like he “done found him a job”. When was the last time you saw a Chiefs’ quarterback zip a pass between two defenders? Face it, Orton is the “O” factor and should be expected to help the Chiefs this week. And if things work out against Oakland, then the new Chiefs with the “O’ factor will return to Denver, against the team that cut him four weeks ago. Speaking of Oakland, will the Chiefs make a serious run for the playoffs? Let’s see what the Monday Niters think. Now, be sure to look for what Booker said.Dr. Charles Allen: The new coach, Romeo Crennel, has created a new culture in the Chiefs’ organization. That culture led to a big, unexpected showing against Green Bay. The formidable Packers were not looking for a tough game against the Chiefs. But the Chiefs came through, just like Charles said they would. Chiefs by 10Paul “the Converted Apostle” Booker: Booker says the change in attitude among the players is remarkable. They just wouldn’t play for Todd the Tyrant. Like Patti LaBelle, the Chiefs now have a “new attitude”. And because of that, Booker is picking the Chiefs over Oakland. Do you believe it?He is parting waves with “that” Ike and  has accepted the Chiefs as winners. Praise the Lord. Chiefs by 7Carl Clark: Carl still thinks the Chiefs were lucky last Sunday, against Green Bay. Even though the Chiefs controlled the ball longer, sacked Aaron Rodgers several times, and even scored on two long drives. Still, Carl is not convinced and he has now taken on Booker’s old role, as a “hater”.  Oakland by 7 Congressman Cleaver: Cleaver is still in Washington, trying to get the Republicans to pass a tax-cut bill for the middle class. In fact, they are about to make “Rev.” mad. That’s because Rev. wants all of us to pay less payroll taxes and the Republicans are holding it up. And it is driving Rev insane with this kind of duplicity. Anyway, Rev is convinced the Chiefs played well and will probably do the same against the Raiders. . . so. . . Chiefs by 7Ike “Oldest Grench Alive” Gardner: Ike enjoyed talking to Mrs. Myla Banks. He even smiled a time or two, during the ten-minute conversation. That made him say later that he was glad that dumb-ass Haley was no longer coaching the Chiefs. And he kind of sighed when he learned that his long-time-hater-ally,  Booker had been converted to the Chiefs. That made him mad and he again denounced the Chiefs. . .what’s new?. . .Oakland by 10Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd says that Green Bay just under-estimated the Chiefs. It is refreshing to see the Chiefs playing as a team. They have recovered quickly from “Haley-itis”, which led them to mess up and not score. Lloyd is cautiously optimistic about the Chiefs winning the next two games. . .but starting Saturday. . . it is the. . . Chiefs by 3Ollie “Dr. Death” Hubbard: Just the other day, Applejack Matthews commented that Ollie is among the world’s most informed obituary experts. And Ollie is not yet sounding the death alarm for the Chiefs. He thinks that this is just the beginning of a “new day” for the Chiefs. He is sending a loud message to his cousin, Faye, in Oakland. Chiefs by 5Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: There was a song by the Persuaders, called “ A Thin Line Between Love And Hate”. That’s how I feel about the Chiefs...you like ‘em one minute and hate ‘em the next. But last Sunday, no one hated the Chiefs. People everywhere were praising them, just like the were the new “David”, slaying Goliath Green Bay. More important, Romeo Crennel looks like he “done found a job too”. But he gotta win Christmas Eve against Oakland and New Year’s Day out at Denver. . . he will, at least this Saturday at Arrowhead. Chiefs by 6Ed “Always Right” West: Ed never got over hiring a golf coach to coach pro football. You will remember Haley was a golf coach at one time and Ed has never supported him. But Ed is quick to praise Crennell for his philosophy includes both the offense and defense. Coming from a real football player, Ed is again right, especially about Romeo’s Christmas gift to the fans. Chiefs by 7Eric “Last Second Christmas Shopper” Wesson: It is just hard to gauge what the Chiefs are going to do. They play so inconsistent. They allow Miami, which had not one any games, come in and beat them soundly. Then they send Green Bay packing in a game they really had no chance, on paper, of winning. But, I suppose a quarterback and coach will make a difference. The Chiefs, will beat the Raiders by 10. Get Romeo’s three-year contract ready.

paragraphs.text: Chiefs, Not At All Like Beyonce

frames.text: Chiefs, Not At All Like Beyonce

paragraphs.text: Beyonce in her new album says “I woke up like this”. That means she was not taught, nor did she acquire any of her great talents. Inferentially, she is saying that she was “born” with such entirety. Let’s see how that applies to the Chiefs, after their rather surprising win over Miami. But before that, let’s record what happened over to Paul Booker’s house recently.

First, we talked about the upcoming community conversation about Health. Sponsored by the Healthcare Foundation, this big conversation will take place on October 11, down at the Sheraton Hotel in Crown Center. Everyone can come but you must register. More important, all of the Monday Niters will be there, expressing their views on behalf of the central city elderly. So, the guys just gave a sample of the things they will promote and say, during this high-tech conversation.

Dr. Charles Allen and Paul Booker want to see more health programs, addressing mental health and Alzheimer’s disease.  And Ike Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield and Carl Clark expressed the critical need to address diabetes. They say that this diabetes thing is rampant and will speak collectively for those thousands of uncontrolled diabetics. And Ed West chimes in about the need for nursing home reform and the lack of adequate health insurance among our elderly brothers and sisters. In fact, the Monday Niters will be working with elderly organizations like the Palestine Senior Citizens Center to get their support. It is the goal to have fifty central city elderly persons at that conference. The business, at hand, is clear.
Speaking of business, the guys started reminiscing again. Last week, it was about health care providers. This year, they switched to entrepreneurs of the past.

Here are some of the names that emerged from the early Kansas City days:. G.L. Blankenship (beauty products); George and Ollie Gates (barbq); Madame C. J. Walker (cosmetics); Fannie Meeks (funeral services); Sarah Rector (real estate); Everett O’Neal (security); Earl Pitts (tire company); Leon Arnold (real estate); Chuck Wimes (mortgage lending);  and Roy Walker (electrician). These brave men and women really set the tone for Kansas City’s rise to international fame and are the maverick heroes of our past.

Speaking of heroes, the Chiefs had several, last week in their win over Miami. Knile Davis ran wild, making us think that Jamaal Charles had better get well quick. And certainly, McKnight was a pleasant surprise, catching two touchdown passes. And the defense showed that there is some hope that they will jell, some day. But the real message is not at all like Beyonce’s. The Chiefs were not born,  like they played Saturday. It is and has been a struggle, every step of the way. Eleven starters hurt. A bunch of undrafted  no-names. A highly-paid but inconsistent quarterback. An ineffective offensive line. All of this adds up to a severe lack of “entirety”. Up till now, the Chiefs could and would not impress Beyonce, at all.

Now, Denver and Seattle have that Beyonce-like- entirety, displaying “seasoned excellence”, on every down and every Sunday. The Chiefs only have to dream about this kind of play. So let’s not get too happy over last Sunday’s win. That’s because the New England Patriots  will be coming to town Monday, playing the Chiefs before a nationally televised audience. And they Patriots will be playing like Beyonce sings and dances, repeating to themselves often  that “they woke up like this”.

Like Mila Banks, we all hope the Chiefs will continue upward. But who knows about those Chiefs? They are quite “sometimey” and they can change in a New York minute. But, here’s what the guys think will happen at Arrowhead on Monday night:
Dr. Charles Allen      Patriots are not what they used to be
Chiefs by 10
Mila Banks                 Really hope this winning continues
Chiefs  by 10
Paul Booker              The Brady factor is real
Patriots by 14
Carl Clark                  KC’s offensive line is still limited
Patriots by 14
Bubba Cleaver         By Tuesday morning, both teams are 2-2
Chiefs by 10
Ike Gardner             Little boys are not ready for the Big Boys
Patriots by 17
Lloyd Greenfield    On a wing and a prayer
Chiefs by 10
Ollie Hubbard         Like Donna Summers, K.C. will survive
Chiefs by 7
Jim Nunnelly          Like Jay Z, the Chiefs find  the Holy Grail
Chiefs by 3
Ed West                  Offensive weapons return
Chiefs by 1

paragraphs.text: Matt Cassel is in trouble. He is injured and he will never know if his likely benching is because of that injury or just inept play. It doesn’t matter because “it is what it is”.

He was well on his way to being benched anyway. And we all know it. And the Monday Niters spent half their meeting session, discussing Matt Cassel. But before we share some crushing comments, let’s look into the non-news-making aspects of this week’s game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
Here are some interesting and provocative facts you should know before watching Sunday’s game in Tampa Bay.

First, Jamaal Charles is first in the NFL in rushing (no surprise). Justin Huston, Chiefs’ defensive standout is tied for third in quarterback sacks. Tampa Bay’s starting quarterback is Josh Freeman, a graduate of Grandview High school.

Tampa Bay beat the Oakland Raiders in the Super Bowl, just after the 2002 regular season. Bo Jackson refused to play for Tampa Bay, even though he was the first round draft choice. Doug Williams, first African American to quarterback a Super Bowl, was also a first-round pick for Tampa Bay.
In 1978, Trent Green, Chiefs quarterback under Dick Vermeil, also suffered a season-ending concussion. And that brings us back to Matt Cassel’s, boo-producing injury, last Sunday against Baltimore.
Here’s what the Monday Niters remarked, along with their predictions for the must-win game against Tampa Bay.

Dr. Charles Allen: Believes that if Eric Winston had been doing his job, Cassel wouldn’t have gotten hurt in the first place. Case of sour grapes. Dr. Allen also foresees a coaching change in the near future. Oh?       Chiefs by 7

Paul Booker: believes that Matt Cassel was just looking for a way to sit down and take a 60-million dollar rest break...and thereby avoid a lot of bad press. However, Booker says that the hometown boy, Josh Freeman, has no respect for his hometown team. . .thus. . .Tampa Bay by 7

Carl Clark: is truly sorry that Cassel had to get hurt. So he blames the coaches for not taking Cassel out of the game in the first place. Either way, the Chiefs will give the fans “the same old Mitt, warmed over”. . . Tampa Bay by 10

Congressman Emanuel Cleaver: Is busy campaigning. But he did take time out to meet with a few sports fans last Sunday, after the Baltimore game. He spoke candidly about his new-found status in Washington, after having become the chairman of the Congressional Black Caucus. Being a part of a privileged few, he talks weekly with President Obama and goes all over the country in his behalf. But when it comes to the Chiefs, he is embarrassed by their sub-mediocre play. But still stays faithful. . .Chiefs by 7

Ike Gardner: Is nearly 95  years old and has been a Chiefs’ season ticket holder, longer than Winston has been alive. Saying forcefully, he has never witnessed Kansas City fans booing any injured player.
But toward this Sunday’s game, Ike says the Chiefs have talent but have incompetent coaches. . .thus, Tampa Bay by 12

Lloyd Greenfield: Is mad at Eric Winston, recently acquired offensive lineman. Lloyd says he’s been going out to the games for years and he thinks it is unjust and out of place for a player (Winston) to make such a comment. As for this Sunday, Lloyd is afraid they are killing Jamaal Charles, by running him so often and under such impossible circumstances.....but he still remains hopeful. . .Chiefs by 3

Ollie Hubbard:  doesn’t believe that crowd was cheering AGAINST Matt Cassel but they were cheering FOR Brady Quinn. Nonetheless, the fact remains, the Chiefs are lacking in quarterback play. That makes Ollie get down on his knees at Ebenezer and pray. . .Chiefs by 3

Jim Nunnelly: thinks that all the national media coverage is severely overblown and highly sensationalized. Worthless and idle chatter, allowing a newbie like Winston to get some press. The real issue is that Matt Cassel has not played well enough to win. Huston, Johnson, Hali, Charles, Berry again spectacular. . .Chiefs by 6

Ed West: Believes the offense will finally catch up with the defense, especially with a new quarterback. He strongly feels that Cassel was “put” in a bad situation because of horrible coaching (Ed may have something)....nonetheless.....Chiefs by 3

Eric “Amanda, Bri, and Erica’s Dad” Wesson: Asks the question, Does Clark Hunt ever think, in the back of his mind, “Am I’m paying this guy to throw complete passes to the other team. Throw the passes to the guys in the red uniforms you dummy.” .... Chiefs by 3 in overtime

paragraphs.text: This past Monday night, we talked a whole lot. A lot went down this week. Especially with the Chiefs’ victory and  the murder-suicide tragedy piercing the nation’s headlines. But, before we get to that, we had some community-minded guests to join us. One was Tony G from Hot 103 and the others were the Go-Along Club and Andre Jackmon, a supervisor in the Behavioral Health department at Swope Health Services. Thus, we want to tell you a little about them and then comment on Romeo’s leadership, through a double-crisis week with his team.

• TONY G. . . for 19years, this young man has led the Toy and Food Drive for all of Kansas City. For this effort, he has been awarded boundless recognition but he still presents as eager as if it’s the very first time.

Many don’t know but Tony G  was a credible basketball player in the old Catholic leagues. Moreover, his name carried forwarded to the radio airways and he is featured each morning in “drive time”, delivering a morning start for thousands of metropolitan residents. He has also assisted in the development of the popular teen talk show, Generation Rap on Hot 103. But for Tony, this annual food event is just being a good neighbor. Having grown up near 39th and Prospect, Tony G just gives back to his community. In fact, he demonstrates his commitment year after year, making sure that families have food and kids have toys for Christmas. Big kudos for Tony G.

• THE GO ALONG CLUB. . . This is group of middle-aged men who get together frequently. However, social-minded the group may appear, they raise thousands of dollars each year for college scholarships. They too were on-hand to talk about their community service, especially providing worthy students with money to go to college....raised through their own corporate resources. We cannot say enough about the men who help our community...each and every day.

• ANDRE JACKSON, SWOPE HEALTH SERVICES. . . starting out as just a worker, Andre is now a supervisor in the Behavioral Health department. Andre is involved in establishing counseling and case management services, in and around schools. So far, he has mobilized many agencies and most important, helped his agency get services to those who need it. Andre is one of the rising young men in our community who defy the inappropriate stereotype of young black men. Andre called on us Monday Niters and the others to assist our children, even if just saying an encouraging word. He reiterated that our young people want and need our help.

Well, what a night for Monday Niters. . . to hear and see our men, stepping up to help out in their community. Also, there was a lot of conversation about the Chiefs. Mainly, about Romeo and how he handled a team, wrought with confusion caused by the suicide of one  of the their fellow players. One that also included a murder of the player’s girlfriend. And one that required getting that team ready to play a game, the next day. So, we took a poll among our members and guests and commented on Romeo Crennel’s finest moment in his profession. On Sunday, Romeo will take his team back to his former place of employment, Cleveland. Where he once coached the Browns and now will return a national hero. Here’s what we think:
Dr. Charles Allen:     Romeo was quite admirable this week.                   Chiefs by 7
Paul Booker: He was outstanding handling all that pressure.   Browns by 10
Carl Clark: He did a good job but he didn’t save his.                 Browns by 10
Ike Gardner: He held it together. Because of that, I will pay  his bus fare to his next job. Browns by 3
Lloyd Greenfield:     He handled the situation, using family values.        Browns by 3
Jim Nunnelly: God must love Romeo. Chiefs by 7
Ed West: His demeanor saved the Chiefs....and his job.        Chiefs by 3
Joe Webster: Romeo earned himself one more year.                  Chiefs by 3
Andre Jackmon:     Romeo handled the media well...go Raiders         no prediction
Hadley Reimal:     Admirable job under difficult circumstances.            Chiefs by 3
Ron Walton:           Return to Cleveland will return him to reality.             Browns by 10
Sanders Martin: Romeo should be back next year.                                Browns by 7
Willie Humphrey: Romeo did a helluva job getting the team up.           Browns by 7
Tom Brown: Romeo fate is still shaky, despite a good week. Browns by 7

paragraphs.text: If you are up till 9, on Thursday nights, no doubt you have become addicted to the tv drama series, called “Scandal”. It stars Kerry Washington, a black female who operates in and about Washington and all the mess.

However, she is both part of and solution to all the drama, surrounding those who seek and own world power. This chick is bad, yall. She has total access to the President and yet flaunts her courage, wherever and whenever someone needs it. paragraphs.text: Apogee is a word, used in astronomy to describe the farther point out there in space. It was used in the novel, Fifty Shades Of Grey to describe the best feeling that can be derived from romantic encounter. Well, on Sunday, the apogee of football games will be played in New Orleans. This game will feature Baltimore Ravens and the San Francisco Forty Niners.

San Francisco will probably win, mainly because of its stellar quarterback, Kaepernick. This kid is “on fire” and will silence the tirades and mental health outbreaks of Ray Lewis. Ray can stir up the crowd but this kid can move the ball down the field. In fact, over half of his passes go for twenty yards or more. His actions speak louder than Ray Lewis’ words. He is arguably the best quarterback in the league.

Speaking of quarterbacks, why can’t the Chiefs buy, borrow or beg for a good quarterback? Other teams do this but Kansas City cannot get it done. That’s why the Chiefs are “left out” and left at home. You would think that a team with six Pro Bowlers can at least find one quarterback, among all these youngsters. And they are not promising that the quarterback position is not their highest draft priority. That attitude is just plain stupid and explains why the Chiefs haven’t been in a Superbowl, since 1970.
So while San Francisco and Baltimore will be kicking it in the SuperDome, the Kansas City Chiefs will be looking wise and otherwise and missing the point.
In the words of Herm Edwards, you play to win the game. Something the Chiefs don’t understand. They need some apogee. . . or something.
Here’s what the Monday Niters think:
Dr. Charles Allen:  San Francisco by 14...no doubt about it.
Paul Booker: Ravens by 7  Ray Lewis will sack Jim Harbaugh for a second time.
Carl Clark: San Francisco by 14 Kaepernick will outperform Flacco
Ike Gardner: San Francisco by 7 They have an excellent offense and defense.
Lloyd Greenfield: Sam Francisco by 7 Just watch them go.
Ollie Hubbard: San Francisco by 12 Going with the City by the Bay.
Jim Nunnelly: San Francisco by 10 Smith will make Raytown proud.
Ed West: San Francisco by 10 Just wait and see.
Eric Wesson: San Francisco by 14. Just watch those Young Bloods operate.
Tracy Allen (sports editor): San Francisco by 7 While this will be the last hooray for Ray Ray, his offense won’t help him.

paragraphs.text: Marvin Gaye is best known for his smash hit song, “Let’s Get It On”. But my favorite, Marvin Gaye song is “Inner City Blues”. In this seventies song, Marvin highlights what it’s like to be an outsider and a non-participant in the American dream. In fact, at one point in the song he screams. . . “makes me want to holler and throw up both my hands”.

Well, given the last few seasons, the Chiefs have sure made a lot of fans “holler and throw up both hands. But, there is a new sheriff and deputies in town and let’s just wait and see what if we can lower our collective hands. Okay, it was important for me to say that first.

Speaking of importance, the Monday Niters were special guests of the Kansas City Chiefs this past Tuesday. Yes, the Chiefs treated us like we were royalty up at their training camp in St. Joseph.  They gave us special parking passes, covered and cool sideline seating, lots of beverages, and a ton of material. . . all to emphasize that the 2012 Chiefs are no longer alive. They are dead. And in their place are notables like a new quarterback, Alex Smith and a first-picked, first-round offensive lineman named Eric Fisher. The new coach, Andy Reid, walked around the field like he had “star-trek” hope for these new, improved Chiefs. Joining from the past are the exciting Jamaal Charles, at running back and Dwayne Bowe, acrobatic receiver. This mix of old and new will get its first opportunity-to-impress tonight, against the New Orleans Saints, in a doesn’t-count, preseason game.

But it does count for the Chiefs. If the Chiefs should lose, the fans will “holler” louder than before. And the renewed promise of a “new day” will slipper into the usual “hang-ups, let-downs, bad breaks, and set-backs”. And of course, there will be a designated player, appointed to tell the fans why we should believe that the Chiefs still deserve our support and that they “will” be better than last year’s 2-14 record. But, oh if they win!

The “holler” will be converted into “screaming for joy”. The hang-ups will be reduced. The let-downs will be lifted up. The bad breaks will be forgiven. And the set-backs will be forgotten. And we will look forward to the regular season, with “red colors” draped all over us.
But, like a line in Marvin Gaye’s song says, “only God knows where the Chiefs are headed”.
We sure don’t.

Monday Niters who were VIPs at the Chiefs’ training camp, August 6 included Dr. Charles Allen, Paul Booker, Carl Clark, Ike Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield, Jim Nunnelly and Ed West. Also on the guest list were Robert Allen, Clancy Parker, Joe Webster, Sanders Martin, and Ron Walton.

paragraphs.text: Carl Clark was in the Navy and travelled extensively. That introduction to the world has netted him many friends and benefits. In fact, he earned the nickname “Sweet Pea” because he is generally a likeable guy.
Because of that, he is well known across the metropolitan area, especially in social circles. He is the “grand-master of the 6902 Club” and has served as president of the prestigious Ivanhoe Club.

But, his real passion is the safety of children. You can see him any day at Fifty First and Main, caring for the children who have to cross the street to Visitation Catholic school. For doing such a good job and being well-liked, he is known as the “priest of safety”. Since 1995, he has been there on that corner, doing what he feels is his calling....protecting the kids from predators and crazy drivers.
But, Carl is best known for his role in the Monday Niters, He is so opinionated that his fellow friends are noting that he is getting more like that Ike Gardner, everyday.

Carl, who used to support the Chiefs is now voting against them, week after week. In fact, he said the Chiefs will not win more than five games this season. To his chagrin,the Chiefs have already won four and are looking any day for that fifth victory. .So at his house Monday night, everyone was kidding Carl about the above picture....that shows him holding up the number “five”.
Like other doubters, Carl is having to rethink his early predictions and yet he holds to his prediction and says the Chiefs will lose to Tennessee Titans by a field goal..
Except for Ike, his fellow Monday Niters disagree. Let’s now look in and see what the rest of the guys think.

Dr. Charles Allen: Doc is still concerned about this Alzheimer’s disease. Particularly, he is warning all care-givers that it takes more than “24-7” to look after those, with Alzheimer’s. But he is quite optimistic about the Chiefs, especially the coaching aspect. Thus, he sees Sunday as another victory for Kansas City. Chiefs by 7.

PAUL BOOKER:  Interested in all the violence, Booker has high praise for Jackson County. The County has just released a plan to curtail some of the violence and he is elated about that. And he’s happy about the Chiefs being 4-0. He says it is strictly because of those linebackers....Hali, Houston and Johnson. Chiefs by 10

Bubba Cleaver: He is up to his neck in dealing with the government “shutdown” in Washington. He attends every session, hoping for a resolution. . . but there is definitely a war going on in the nation’s capital.. But Cleaver is keeping the faith and still earning national respect, every day. Just like the Chiefs. No doubt about Sunday.  Chiefs by 7.

Ike “Out of Control” Gardner: Ike is intelligent, committed but cantankerous as hell. He flatout disagrees with everybody, except his current and past St. James pastors, both Rev. and E-3.  He did say a few nice things about Dontari Poe, the Chiefs defensive nose guard. But, he was Ol’ Ike when it came to the outcome, Tennessee by 3.

Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd, unlike painful Ike, is a mild-mannered, thoughtful guy. He feels that educated people are more effective, when they share their talents with lesser educated people. This “team” approach will make the city, better for everyone. Further, he is pleased with the Chiefs’ team play and Jamaal Charles in particular. They will shine again in Tennessee Sunday. Chiefs by 7

Ollie Hubbard: Big Hub is one of Lincoln University’s greatest advocates. If Lincoln is having a fundraiser, Ollie will call you at 3 a.m., to remind you of your “forced” promise to buy a ticket to a Lincoln event. That dedication has earned him many friends. Just like his wisdom in supporting the Chiefs, this Sunday. Chiefs by 7

Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly:  He is really gung-ho about this mental health and violence stuff. His family is running from him because he is urging them to get involved in this community issue. His grandson, Christian, says his grandfather is all about “liberating mental health”. In fact, he notes a mental uplift in the Chiefs. The special teams are leading the way., including this Sunday. Chiefs by 7

Ed West: He keeps wondering why local  control of the police department keeps coming up. With people leading the board like Alvin Brooks, Ed asks “what’s the problem”? He is asking that about the Chiefs, as well. With special teams scoring points and getting good field position. . . what’s the problem?. . . thus, Chiefs by 10.

paragraphs.text: Bright Lights, Big City And The 9-1 Chiefs

frames.text: Bright Lights, Big City And The 9-1 Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Do you remember that old time blues song, “Bright Lights, Big City”?

Well, this was a song that was sung by a man from a small town, who was crying about his girlfriend, who had gone to the “big city” and no longer needed or loved him. In fact, the song says….”bright lights and big city, they went to my baby’s head”.

And that’s exactly what happened to the Chiefs last Sunday night. All the hype and national headlines just messed the Chiefs up. Here’s a 2-14 team last year, hearing daily how they lost all last year and now are on top of the entire National Football League and undefeated on top of that.

That was just too much for the Chiefs to handle.  They got caught up in the “bright lights” and lost badly to Denver. Now, let’s hope they return to normal and beat the 4-6 San Diego Chargers. Now, that the lights have been turned off, let’s see if they can win number 10 out at Arrowhead Sunday.

But big praise should go to Ike Gardner and Carl Clark, for seeing through all the hype, They knew the Chiefs would fold, with the eyes of the world on them. So, we all had to kiss their rings for seeing through the “offense-less” Chiefs. .

So the song, “Bright Lights, Big City” set off a conversation about the singers of the fifties, sixties and seventies. It was remarkable how sharp these old minds were in remembering all the artists of days gone by.

Some of those top names were, Sonny Thompson, Lula Reed, Ruth Brown, Etta James “Annie Had A Baby” by Hank Ballard and the Midnighters, ”I Only Have Eyes For You” by the Flamingoes, Lou Rawls, Johnny Taylor and Sam Cooke all former lead singers from the gospel group, the Soul Stirrers, Fontella Bass, Little Willie John and “Fever”, Ike and Tina Turner,  Jackie Wilson’s “Lonely Teardrops”, Fats Domino and The Dominoes, The Moonglows. and on and on.

Before you knew it, we were all drifting back so far…that we either fell asleep or forgot we came to watch a football game and talk about the Chiefs and their first loss.  Then we woke up and remembered that we had to make our predictions. Here’s how we think Sunday’s game will go.
Dr. Charles Allen:   Embarrassed, but K.C. will beat the Chargers.Chiefs by 14
Mrs. Mila Lewis Banks: Going to Kansas City, here I come. Chiefs by 7
Paul Booker: Phillip will be sent up the Rivers. Chiefs by 10
Carl Clark, Denver exposed K.C’s weaknesses. Chargers by 7
Ike Gardner: Don’t worry about the alligator in the pond down the road. Chargers by 7 When your foot is in the middle of a snake pit.
Lloyd Greenfield: K.C. has a debt to pay and they will settle it. Chiefs by 7
Ollie Hubbard: Praying for Kansas City, Chiefs by 3
Jim Nunnelly:  I know it’s gonna work out fine (Ike Turner). Chiefs by 17
Ed West: Welcome home to the 12th man (the crowd). Chiefs by 7 City……………………………….Chiefs by 3

paragraphs.text: Nat ‘King’ Cole, The Christmas
Song, And The 10-3 Chiefs

frames.text: Nat ‘King’ Cole, The Christmas Song, And The 10-3 Chiefs

paragraphs.text: For those of you under 50, you probably missed a treat, not hearing all the songs ever recorded by Nat “King”Cole.

Every year about this time, that smooth, velvety voice makes its way into our ears, hearts, and mind. And for us over fifty, we recall that Ol’ King Cole was the very first African American to host his own tv show. Now, that’s something. Belting out songs like, “You Send Me” and of course, no one can forget, “Unforgettable”.

But, the song that keeps on giving and selling is “The Christmas Song”. Now you may like Mary J. Blige and Johnny Mathis and even Donnie Hathaway. But none can top Ol’ King Cole when it comes to validating the coming of Christmas.

Now for us in Kansas City, we are splitting our time between getting ready for Christmas and getting our Chiefs ready for the playoffs. Baltimore and Miami are like us, waiting for the final word that they are “in the running for the February Super Bowl”. But teams places like Oakland and Tennessee and even Atlanta are singing along, with Nat King Cole and his perennial, “Christmas Song”. That’s all they can sing about, through now.

So for us, the song ought to be a reminder that the 10-3 Chiefs are back and have recovered from a dismal last year. Most important, we have proved that Booker and Cantankerous Ike Gardner wrong. They said the Chiefs would not win more than five games this and already they have doubled that. So, I wish they could create a Christmas Song that would memorialize those kind of doubters. Perhaps we could call it, “Wrong Way Ike” and, “Poor, Pitiful Paul”.

But thank God for the rest who have/had faith in the Kansas City Chiefs. They can now say proudly that “yes, there is a Santa Claus” and croon along with Nat “King” Cole, at the same time. It’s beginning to look a lot like Christmas. Let’s hear from the rest of the guys.

paragraphs.text: You all remember Flip Wilson. He had his own television show, way back in the sixties. In fact, he was one of the first African American comedians to have a major white following. Most people will remember him as “Geraldine”, a cross-dressed character he created for the show. Everyone like ol’ Flip and he sure did a lot to reduce racial tensions, nationwide. Everyone waited for and watched Flip Wilson do his thing on Sunday evenings.

Speaking of doing things, the Chiefs failed to win, out at Arrowhead this last Sunday. But don’t fret too much because they will be still be playing after they play Sunday against the Chargers.. That simply means they have played well enough and won enough games to “qualify” for the Super Bowl chase.

However, two things. They have to win to stay in the mix. And secondly, they have to play on the road. Now, remember when the Chiefs won the Super Bowl after the 1969 season, they were in the same position. They were a wild card entry, which means they can pursue the Super Bowl….but they have to play on the road. If you want to know more about the only Super Bowl the Chiefs have played in, just ask Ike Gardner. He is still mad because the Chiefs have never regained the respect they once had, when they won the “big game” against the Joe Kapp and the Minnesota Vikings.

Speaking of Ike and his cantankerous ways, I owe him somewhat of an apology. You will remember last week, I talked about how Ike had consistently beat up on the Chiefs. In spite of them winning eleven games this year, he still insists they are a mediocre team at best. Truthfully, they are much more than they were last year. But last Sunday against Indianapolis , they stunk. I mean less than mediocre. After the first series touchdown, the Chiefs went downhill, the rest of the game. Thatcaused national commentators to talk badly about the Chiefs, as well. They say that the Chiefs can’t win against teams with winning tradition and records.

That sounds like what Ike has been saying. Really, I don’t mind what Ike says. I just don’t like the way he says it. There’s no love or loyalty in his cantankerous comments. He sounds so disloyal. Unlike other Monday Niters like Dr. Allen, Paul Booker, Carl Clark, Bubba Cleaver, Lloyd Greenfield, Ollie Hubbard and Ed West, Ike just blatantly “tells it like it is”. And readers everywhere just are appalled at his non-support of the home team.

But another old saying may apply. “It is what it is”. The Chiefs are shaky some days. But some days, they show great promise, especially among players like Derrick Johnson and Jamaal Charles and even Tamba Hali. Another old saying is that “you can’t make a silk purse out of a pig’s ear”. That means you have to accept what the Chiefs are and they are a good team…but not a great team like New England or Denver or New Orleans or even Seattle. Ike would say the Chiefs will not make it through the first round in the playoffs. But they made it this far and they will be trying to advance. And they will be on tv, when most teams will be watching.

Getting back to tv, we started out talking about Flip Wilson having his own tv show, way back when. And like all of our favorite shows, something is said that sticks with us all of our life. And it just may well wrap up this conversation about the Chiefs. Old Flip used to say somewhere during every telecast. What You See Is What You Get”
And that my friends describes our Kansas City Chiefs. So Ike needs to call on Flip to help him state his disdain, more appropriately.

paragraphs.text: George Jefferson, Fantasies And The 11-5 Chiefs

frames.text: George Jefferson, Fantasies And The 11-5 Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Do you remember “The Jeffersons”?

That was a tv show that appeared regularly on CBS, way back in the seventies. This was a Norman Lear production, that attempted to show that black people were “moving on up”. In fact, the show took place in the Jeffersons’ Fifth Avenue apartment, on the upper East Side of New York City. And since the prosperity was all new to the Jeffersons, the writers traced their humorous, everyday activities. Some of it was funny but the whole thing was filled with a lot of fantasy.

Speaking of fantasy, the Chiefs have been living on “Fantasy Island”. For the first nine games the Chiefs were the ‘talk of the sports world”. They were undefeated until they met the Payton-laced Denver Broncos. Then the Chargers. Then, the Broncos again. And just like that, the little “fantasy” bubble began to bust. In fact, these same Chiefs lost five of their next seven games, the latest being to the Chargers last Sunday. Talk about up and down. The Chiefs were living in a fantasy world and it all came tumbling down, causing many to mentally eliminate the Chiefs from further contention.

But is it over for the Chiefs? Now remember the Chiefs were 2-14 in 2013. And now they are in playoffs and have been there solidly for three weeks running. They didn’t need help from other teams, they clinched a spot and just waited. So, my point is that the “fantasy” continues, in spite of them losing the last third of the season. And last Sunday, they lost but they didn’t use twenty of the first twenty two starters. So, San Diego beat the second and third teamers of the Chiefs. Not Jamaal Charles or Tamba Hali or Derrick Johnson or Dwayne Bowe.

So what’s the point? The most salient point is that the Chiefs are still pursuing the NFL Super Bowl game.. Even Carl Clark says let’s support the Chiefs “for the heck of it”. As always, that Paul Booker and Ike Gardner are non-supportive, believing that the Chiefs will lose their first round playoff game to Indianapolis Colts, just like they did a couple of weeks ago.And for sure, that will be “it” for Kansas City and its fantasy season.

Hold up for a minute!. The Chiefs did put eight players on the All-Pro roster. And their coach, Andy Reid, will probably be Coach Of The Year. And some second teamers are going to playing a lot, come Sunday afternoon. Thereby, making the Chiefs even better prepared for the upcoming game.

Bottom line, like the Jeffersons. . . the Chiefs are “moving on up”. They finally got a piece of the NFL pie. Now Ike will probably predict against the Chiefs. But you all know Ike. He was wrong eleven of sixteen times this year. That means he wasn’t right, most of the time, about the Chiefs. He is not the “Holy Grail” of predicting football games.

So, let’s get behind our hometown team and maybe, just maybe….we can “move further on up” to the East side and take on New England and then onto the West side to take on Denver. Wait. Wait. Wait. I’ve drifted back into Fantasy Land.
For right now, Chiefs over the Colts. (We hope).

paragraphs.text: Chiefs Are Not Pearls. . . More Like Costume Jewelry…

frames.text: Chiefs Are Not Pearls. . . More Like Costume Jewelry…

paragraphs.text: Someone once said that “a pearl is not a pearl, until it comes out of its shell”. That should have become the theme for our Monday night session, down at the Juke House. Congressman Cleaver hosted the event Monday and the evening was full of history lessons. That meant that everyone was cordial to each other (being the first meeting of the season). Then, things turned sour and we began to verbally assault the Chiefs. However before that we spent considerable time, talking about the domestic violence in the NFL, a revered teacher in the Kansas City Public Schools history, and then, we lit in on the Chiefs.

First, about the domestic violence. This subject arose because the news media is going crazy, talking about the elevator video showing Ray Rice beating his girlfriend. Under the new NFL policy, he will be suspended for six games and if a second event occurs, he could be banned “for life”. This week the Baltimore Ravens cut Rice’s contract and the NFL suspended him indefinitely. Let’s go on.

Secondly, we reminisced. Mainly about the “good old days”, when education was truly our number one priority in Kansas City. Jimmy Ray Hubbard said during a recent visit that at one time “Lincoln High School had more master’s level and PhD teachers than any other school. That’s why the guys, especially Ike, Carl, Ed and Lloyd saluted Dr. Jeremiah Cameron, English teacher at Lincoln in the forties and fifties and sixties. Sadly but understandably, some short-sighted people labeled the late Dr. Cameron as “arrogant”. But always  lauded for his teaching skills and his relentless efforts to fully educate our children. And to Jimmy Ray Hubbard’s point, he had a master’s in English from the University of Chicago and an earned PhD from Michigan State University. Now, this “pearl” is/was definitely out of his shell. In fact, it makes us all nostalgic….wishing for the “good old days”, when the quality of our educational system was never in question.

Lastly, we turned to another “pearl” that is nowhere near “out of the shell”. Yes, we all chimed in our luck-less, lifeless Kansas City Chiefs, After the shellacking they received Sunday by Tennessee, Ed West quickly said the Chiefs may only win two games this year. Booker, who is really happy these days, said the Chiefs are not worth a (four letter word). And we were all uniform in believing that Alex Smith is more like “costume jewelry” than a pearl. And everyone is still wondering why Jamaal Charles remained in his shell, all afternoon.

At some point, we all became redundant and as usual, we began to repeat ourselves. So real quickly, the question was asked. . . “how will the Chiefs do against Denver on Sunday”. Well, I’ve never witnessed such laughter in my life. It was like Kat Williams or Kevin Hart had told a funny joke.

Now folks, Denver is saturated with “all kinds of pearls”….Manning, a great offensive line, Vonn Miller, an effective secondaryand on and on. So except for two loyalists, all of us believe the Chiefs will be murdered by the Broncos.
In fact, the mood switched from speaking highly about Dr. Jeremiah Cameron to a relentless cascade of tears for the sad Chiefs. And we left there, with the Chiefs’ pearls, still in their shell……
Dr. Charles Allen. A hope and a prayer. . . . Chiefs by 3
Paul Booker: K.C. cannot tame Denver . . . Denver by 14.
Carl Clark: K.C.  has no offensive line . . . Denver by 21.
Ike Gardner: Weak corners and an even weaker defensive line . . . Denver by 28.
Lloyd Greenfield: No line, no kicker . . . Denver by 14
Ollie Hubbard: Chiefs better perk up . . . Chiefs by 3
Jim Nunnelly:  Not coming out this week . . . Denver by 30
Ed West: K.C. can’t tackle, can’t score . . . Denver by 21
Bubba Cleaver.    2 much Manning 2 manage. . . Denver by 14
Eric Wesson “Erica, E.J. Amanda and Bri’s Dad”:. . . Denver will exploit the middle of the field, the corners, special teams and coaching staff . . . Denver by 28 at least.

paragraphs.text: Brandon Lloyd, Alicia Keys, And The Chiefs

frames.text: Brandon Lloyd, Alicia Keys, And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: Did you hear about the butt-kicking New England handed the league-leading Houston Texans, last Monday night. We gathered over to Ed West’s, to watch what we thought would be a good game. It didn’t happen. The Brady Bunch slaughtered the Texans, 42-14, with Brady tossing four touchdown passes.

On the bright spot is that game was Kansas City’s own, Brandon Lloyd. We remember Brandon’s high school days out at Blue Springs. From there, he went on to star at wide receiver, at the University of Illinois. And then, he has caught passes for the Denver Broncos, the St. Louis Rams and now the New England Patriots. Known for his acrobatic catches, this guy is “on fire”. It is not every receiver who has the best passer in NFL history as his passing mate. Look for more.

Speaking of being “on fire”. Have you heard Alicia Keys’ latest CD, “This Girl Is On Fire”. It is selling like wildfire. If you have seen the video, she paints the story of a young woman, taking on the struggles and joys of life. Not to be outdone, she has to be “on fire”, just to make it. This song has rapidly become the spokes-song for millions of young women, adrift in this world. But, to me, her CD begs the question. . . who is NOT “on fire”. You guessed it. It’s the Kansas City Chiefs. Two buckets of gasoline and a box of matches won’t light up the Chiefs, these days.

They have been down so long that “getting up” don’t even cross their minds. With only two wins again eleven losses, the network commentators don’t even comment on the score, demonstrating their neglect of and disdain for these Chiefs. In fact, talking about the Chiefs was so dull. . . that we found ourselves talking about Robert Griffin III. . . the old time Georgy Burger. . . how integration killed the economic spirit of 18th and 12th streets. . . Tom Brady’s record of a passing touchdown for forty two consecutive games. . . Charles Kynard, premier organist who played at the Blue Room in the sixties...how the post office, the school district and the automotive industry were the plum jobs of the ‘50s, ‘60s, and ‘70s. . . how Carl Clark ignored the state-line boundaries and found Mary Lynn in Kansas City, Kas.

Actually, our discussion had more “fire” than the Chiefs have. In fact, our discussion soon landed into a healthy respect of years-gone-by.  When we were all in one neighborhood and acted and thought unity. When our business owners were our neighbors and our churches were our uniform resource. Yes, when the Chiefs could walk on water, while being “on fire” at the same time. When being from Kansas City was something to behold. . . not to silently mention, in passing. Where did it all go? We don’t know but we wish we had those same pride-filled moments back. And it won’t get any better out in Oakland, this coming Sunday.
The Monday Niters have given up on the Chiefs and all that they stand/stood for. Bottom line, the “fire next time” is a long time away.
Charles Allen: I’m holding on. Chiefs by 3
Paul Booker:  No joy in Muddville.  Raiders by 10
Carl Clark: Chiefs are done!       Raiders by 10
Ike Gardner: Chiefs will lose in the Black Hole. Raiders by 13
Lloyd Greenfield: Chiefs are a broken vessel. Raiders by 14
Ollie Hubbard:  I’m praying at Ebenezer.  Toss-up
Jim Nunnelly: Fire is out for Romeo. Raiders by 7
Ed West: No Bowe, no go!                Raiders by 10

When being from Kansas City was something to behold. . . not to silently mention, in passing. Where did it all go? We don’t know but we wish we had those same pride-filled moments back. And it won’t get any better out in Oakland, this coming Sunday. The Monday Niters have given up on the Chiefs and all that they stand/stood for. Bottom line, the “fire next time” is a long time away.Charles Allen: I’m holding on. Chiefs by 3Paul Booker:  No joy in Muddville.  Raiders by 10Carl Clark: Chiefs are done! Toss-upJim Nunnelly: Fire is out for Romeo. Raiders by 7Ed West: No Bowe, no go!                Raiders by 10

paragraphs.text: Now, let’s get real.  The Chiefs are wishing that Sunday’s game was still pre-season.  That way, they could evaluate the new players, rest the old ones at the end of the first quarter, and then dodge the brutal, candid questions, asked by  blood-sucking reporters after the game.
But, it is “for real” now.  Sunday will open the biggest wound possible in Herm Edwards’ armor.  It will show that the Chiefs are destined for another dismal season.
In addition, Sunday will show that the draft, trades, and  the legacy were all worthless and unfulfilling.

The Chiefs  have too many unknown and untried players, to even think about beating the Patriots.  In fact, we should fast forward this game and go directly to the next two games..against Oakland at home and Atlanta away.  The Chiefs just might beat Oakland, depending on how well Russell, their strong-armed quarterback, plays.  And maybe just maybe we might beat the Vick-less Falcons.  If my math is right, three weeks from now we will be 2-1. But, come Sunday, they will lose so badly that we will think there is another Boston Massacre.  Even those little men on the New England helmets will dance in both end zones.  Tom Brady will pick  our hand-made secondary apart.  And except for a couple of long runs, the Chiefs will appear like they are still in pre-season mode.  Once again, Herm will pick up where he left off, last season.  With an inadequately profound statement that says and does nothing.  And the reporters will laughingly write the same stories that they wrote all  of last year, about how unlikely the Chiefs are to win at all. And the fans will and should direct our attention to  Oakland and Atlanta, the Chiefs’ next two opponents. And Herm will go to work on his next appearance before the reporters, hopefully more realistic.  For now, though. . . look for the Patriots to beat the Chiefs by at least 30 points.
Enough said.

paragraphs.text: Editor, THE CALL:
Each week during football season, I look forward to reading the “Monday Niters” predictions and the commentary by Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly.
Mr. Nunnelly’s commentary in a recent “CALL” issue was particularly interesting as he told a little about each man in the “Monday Nite Footballers group.”
Nunnelly is an excellent writer. He knows how to make words on a page come alive.
Even though the “Monday Niters” lead varied lives with different professions, they enjoy commonalities that make them a cohesive group of remarkable black men.

In a recent  write-up, Nunnelly described these grandfathers of the group from Allen to West as: extraordinary, fantastic, effective, proud, steadfast, remarkable, complete, and encouraging. For what more could one ask?
Monday Niters, “Keep on keeping on.” BRAVO!!.
Terry Strother
Burlington, Iowa

paragraphs.text: Kansas City Chiefs
V. Oakland Raiders
12 p.m. KCTV 5
1-col pix
Charles Allen
The Kansas City Chiefs are playing poorly because of the weak offensive line, never recovering from the loss of Will Shields and Willie Roaf.

Nonetheless, there are some bright spots.  Derrick Johnson and Tamba Hali are both headed to the Pro Bowl, making the new 3-4 defense work.  However, Coach Todd Haley is treating the players like high schoolers rather than the professionals they are.
There is hope for the Chiefs but Haley has to gain a stronger rapport with his players.

paragraphs.text: MONDAY NITER WITH SKILLS . . . Because of his 32years in dentistry, many do not know that Doc is a real genius in the kitchen.  In fact, during the 40 years he has been a member of the Monday Niters, he has always prepared the food for his football cronies.  Here he proudly shows off his baked chicken smothered chicken, laced with rotel tomatoes and black olives.  In addition, he has composed a mixed salad, he calls the “Charley Salad”.  Doc says he learned his culinary skills from having cooked in his parents’ restaurants, down on 18th street.  Always a self-starter, Doc has won the respect of everyone he meets. On top of that, he is one of the loyalists, who always support and vote for the Chiefs.  He is married to Beverly and they have two grown children and a sporty grandson, Robert.

paragraphs.text: LLOYD GREENFIELD

I was a firefighter in this community for over 30 years.  I have seen men and women perform under the worst of disasters.  Thus, knowing about courage and skill is something I have come to expect from every professional, especially those in such high-paid, visible sports professions.  Which brings me to my commentary about our sinking Kansas City Chiefs.

Something is definitely wrong with our team, y’all!  Maybe it’s the management who seems to say it is “my way or the highway”.  Or maybe it is the offensive line, who continually allow the quarterback and running backs no opportunity at all.  I know for sure that the top management is the “weakest link”.

As a firefighter, the chiefs always encouraged, inspired, and supported all of us who were on the frontline.  Not a day went by when we knew we were on the “same team”.  But that is not happening with our Chiefs and the result is a winless season for the Chiefs, joining St. Louis , Tennessee , and Tampa Bay .  But after seeing the game against Dallas , there is some hope, especially among the defensive players. While I haven’t given up, I do believe they will lose again on Sunday against Washington.
Where is the development plan?
Dr. Charles Allen           Chiefs by 10     Redemption!
Paul Booker        Redskins by 13  Eleven good street people desperately needed.
Carl Clark           Redskins by 10  Redskins scalp the Chiefs
Bubba Cleaver       Redskins by 3  Chiefs MIGHT win!
Ike Gardner       Redskins by 13  Too many Indians not enough Chiefs
Lloyd Greenfield   Redskins by 7  The sinking Chiefs!
Ollie Hubbard      Redskins  by 7  More booty kicked
Jim Nunnelly    Chiefs by 3  Chiefs running game emerges
Ed West       Chiefs by 1  They gotta win SOMETIMES!
Eric L. Wesson  Washington by 1  Washington may be just as big of bums as the Chiefs
“The Sports Guy”

frames.text: Monday Niters

paragraphs.text: Where have the legacy gone, the ones on brought on by Buck Buchanan, Willie Lanier, Emmitt Thomas and Otis Taylor?  The Chiefs suck and made us reminsce about the “good old days” when win or lose, fans felt good about our home-town Chiefs.

But after Sunday’s brutal beating by Oakland, we are convinced that the Chiefs could not even beat Raytown Middle School Blue Jays.  And the coaching was as bad as it has ever been.  From the grave, Hank Stram would ask Herm. . . “what the hell are you doing with my team”?  And pulling Larry Johnson from the line-up cashed in any hope we had of winning.

Just don’t know about these Chiefs.  If we put Larry back in the line-up and run him 30 times, we just might win Sunday.  Otherwise, Paul, Carl, Bubba, Ike, Ollie, Lloyd and Ed are right.  Just Charles and I think the legacy will return.  Hopefully!

DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Graduated from UMKC Dental School at age 38. . . gets inward satisfaction from providing needed dental services. . . Catholic by faith. . . a man of a few words but delivers exactly what he promises. . . mentors young professionals. . . known to hang out every once in a while (every dat). . . has never predicted against the Chiefs. . . though he is thoroughly disappointed with but hopeful for the Chiefs. . . Chiefs by 3.

PAUL BOOKER:  Will celebrate his 72nd birthday in November. . . has perfect attendance at the 6902 School. . . believes today’s teenagers are smarter than their parents, which makes the role for grandparents very important. . . has taken an annual physical each year for the past fifty years. . . doesn’t smoke but will take a sip or two or three or four. . . thinks the Chiefs are busted and will not beat the Falcons.. . . no way, no how. . . Atlanta by; 13

CARL CLARK: A Navy veteran...a vice president of the Ivanhoe Club, one of the oldest social clubs in our community. . . planning a trip to Martha’s vineyard. . . went to Indonesia and thought it was Paradise...loves to argue about everything...but no argument about this week’s prediction. . . believes the Chiefs have too many problems to win. . . Atlanta by 14.

BUBBA CLEAVER:  Has three spoiled grandchildren. . . has real inside knowledge on foreclosures. . . played college football with Otis Taylor. . . lives three blocks from the United States Capitol. . . .number one goal is to get Obama elected. . . spends big and...shops furiously at the area’s best thrift stores. . . believes the Chiefs’ snowball is rolling downhill. . . Atlanta by 10.

IKE GARDNER:  Joined the Alphas at Howard University way back in 1954. . . attended Lincoln High School, later taught psychology, math, and science there. . . feels strongly that black men should eat appropriately and exercise regularly. . . has a tendency to tell the same story over and over and over. . . but his story against the Chiefs never changes. . . He says the Chiefs have no offense, no defense, and no coach. . .well all right now, Atlanta by 30.

LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Made sure that the Monday Nite Footballers joined as Life Members of the NAACP. . . s working on purchasing a table at the October 18 annual dinner.. . . spoils his grandchild but not too much. . . wife also a patron of the arts. . . balding beyond belief. . . speaks with authority about the Chiefs’ upcoming loss on Sunday.. . . Atlanta by 7.

JIM NUNNELLY:   Goes by the moniker “Grand Dad”...retiring from Jackson County at the end of year. . . will consult with local organizations afterwards. . . provides the best recommendation letters for teenagers going off to college. . . still will not patronize Shell gas stations because of racial remarks made a 10 years ago. . .has a very quiet demeanor. believes Chiefs should resurrect Larry Johnson and thus, beat Atlanta. . . Chiefs by 3.

ED WEST:  Insisted on sauna in his fantastic house...a body of a 40-year-old (now 70 plus). . . grew up in Osawatomie, Kas. . . one of first African American supervisors at old Western Electric. . . believes that Obama has a chance to win if  he can do something about this economy. . . won a national award for falling asleep the fastest...favorite song “wake me when it’s over”. . . believes the Chiefs cannot win because no offense, no defense, equals no win. . . Atlanta by 10.

Atlanta by 10.IKE GARDNER:  Joined the Alphas at Howard University way back in 1954. . . attended Lincoln High School, later taught psychology, math, and science there. . . feels strongly that black men should eat appropriately and exercise regularly. . . has a tendency to tell the same story over and over and over. . . but his story against the Chiefs never changes. . . He says the Chiefs have no offense, no defense, and no coach. . .well all right now, Atlanta by 30.LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Made sure that the Monday Nite Footballers joined as Life Members of the NAACP. . . s working on purchasing a table at the October 18 annual dinner.. . . spoils his grandchild but not too much. . . wife also a patron of the arts. . . balding beyond belief. . . speaks with authority about the Chiefs’ upcoming loss on Sunday.. . . Atlanta by 7.JIM NUNNELLY:   Goes by the moniker “Grand Dad”...retiring from Jackson County at the end of year. . . will consult with local organizations afterwards. . . provides the best recommendation letters for teenagers going off to college. . . still will not patronize Shell gas stations because of racial remarks made a 10 years ago. . .has a very quiet demeanor. believes Chiefs should resurrect Larry Johnson and thus, beat Atlanta. . . Chiefs by 3.ED WEST:  Insisted on sauna in his fantastic house...a body of a 40-year-old (now 70 plus). . . grew up in Osawatomie, Kas. . . one of first African American supervisors at old Western Electric. . . believes that Obama has a chance to win if  he can do something about this economy. . . won a national award for falling asleep the fastest...favorite song “wake me when it’s over”. . . believes the Chiefs cannot win because no offense, no defense, equals no win. . . Atlanta by 10.

paragraphs.text: Okay. Okay.
The Chiefs are losing and do we need to keep talk about the “dead and buried”?

Many of our Monday Niters have written off the Chiefs for 2008.  Larry Johnson hasn’t helped with his off-the-field shenanigans.  And the lack of an NFL-status quarterback complicates an already dismal season.  And to make matters worse, every one is asking who will the first to get the ax. . . Carl Peterson or Herm Edwards.
To Elize and Clyde in Oakland, I am ready to concede our bet and just not talk about the Chiefs anymore.  So, we Monday Niters talked about the ensuing, history-making election.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN: Charles says he will vote early, on his way into work. . .Charles says his office staff can take as long as it takes to vote. . . is Chiefs are struggling right now, having only a 1-4 record. . .Charles just won’t give up. . .Chiefs by 3
PAUL BOOKER:   Paul will be out of town on November 4. . . he is considering voting absentee on that day. . . Paul believes that the Chiefs are a dysfunctional family. . .Jets by 20.
CARL CLARK:  Carl will vote in the mid-morning, avoiding the on-the-way-to-work rush. . .Carl will never vote again for those Chiefs. . . Jets by 20

BUBBA CLEAVER:   Praised his fellow Monday Niters for being so knowledgeable about election stuff. . .he has helped Obama campaign in Minnesota and Georgia and is being asked to go to Ohio and Arizona soon. . .It IS written that the Chiefs will lose badly in New York. . . Jets by 12

IKE GARDNER:  Ike first voted for Adlai Stevenson way back in 1956. . . he is guaranteeing that his adult children will vote for Obama. . . saying the Chiefs are gathering steam as the roll downhill...Jets by 35.

LLOYD GREENFIELD : Lloyd votes at Grace Point Church at 104th and Blue River Road. . . he will vote electronically. . .thinks we ought to plan a memorial services for the departed Chiefs. . .Jets by 20

OLLIE HUBBARD:  Ollie is the only Monday Niter who has already voted. . . he voted absentee because of his leg disability. . .Ollie always votes for the team that the Chiefs are playing. . .this time, no exception. . . Jets by 40.

JIM NUNNELLY:   He is concerned that people who think they have lost their right to vote. . . if you are awaiting trial in jail and have not been convicted, you can still vote absentee. . . Brett Favre can be beat....Chiefs by 3 (He too is letting the election of Obama get to him!)

ED WEST:   Like Obama, has Kansas connections.. . .he was was born in rural Osawatomie. . . he voted for Kennedy for the first time way back in 1960. . . thinks the Chiefs are an NFL team anymore...no offense, no defense, no win. . . Jets by 30.

paragraphs.text: Editor, THE CALL:
Each week during football season, I look forward to reading the “Monday Niters” predictions and the commentary by Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly.
Mr. Nunnelly’s commentary in a recent “CALL” issue was particularly interesting as he told a little about each man in the “Monday Nite Footballers group.”
Nunnelly is an excellent writer. He knows how to make words on a page come alive.
Even though the “Monday Niters” lead varied lives with different professions, they enjoy commonalities that make them a cohesive group of remarkable black men.

In a recent  write-up, Nunnelly described these grandfathers of the group from Allen to West as: extraordinary, fantastic, effective, proud, steadfast, remarkable, complete, and encouraging. For what more could one ask?
Monday Niters, “Keep on keeping on.” BRAVO!!.
Terry Strother
Burlington, Iowa

paragraphs.text: Chatter, Conversation and Commentary
Super Bowl 42,
No Competition

February is Black History Month. It’s also the month when 22 states will decide its presidential preference. Of lesser importance, it is also the birthday month of our nation’s founding president, George Washington. And for lovers, the month houses Valentine’s Day. But all this will not hold a candle to Super Bowl 42, featuring the undefeated-going-perfect New England Patriots against the never-quitting New York Giants.

But, the game is only a small part. People will be talking about the million-dollar commercials. Already, one sponsor has set aside 16 million to be first in the commercial queue. Add to that the multi-million dollar half-time show (people are still talking about the Janet Jackson fiasco). And most of all, folks are lining the pockets of the Las Vegas casinos. . . rying to pick a for-sure winner. Right now, New England has the edge and everybody is talking about the Brady to Toomer nexus. But what about Little, less-famous brother Eli Manning.

Now, that is the real story of this Super Bowl. For nearly ten years, everybody has been talking about Big Brother, Priceless Peyton. And for  the record, he was supposed to lead the Colts into Phoenix. Instead, it was Eli who is going to the Big Ball. There is hope for us all. Which brings me to my real message about the Monday Nite Footballers Group.

As we all elderize, we can go back to Super Bowl One and Four and any other. We saw Doug Williams set a Super Bowl record for most touchdowns scored in a Super Bowl. We’ve even witnessed running backs like Terrell Davis gallop from one end of the stadium to the other. We’ve known Kansas Citians, like Ralph Brown, who always went to the Super Bowl.

And finally, we remembered way back when the Chiefs were in the Super Bowl. I believe it was against Minnesota. I believe it was Otis Taylor who starred that day. He made a little kick going into the end zone.
Pardon us for not being sure about all the details. . . for it has been 39 years since the Chiefs were there. Hint. Hint. Do you hear us, Peterson and Edwards?

paragraphs.text: Watch for the Tyler Thigpen shirts to start emerging.
After all, this boy is the “only” hopes for our pitiful Chiefs.  He not only is helping the Chiefs on the field but is helping Carl and Herm keep their jobs.
All of a sudden, the Chiefs went from a “last place” team to a “team in the process of re-building”.  And for the record, Larry Johnson better watch out.

We all have seen people who get so big in the head that they think the world can’t operated without them.  Well, even though the Chiefs are still losing, they don’t look as bad in their losing effort.  They have a little swagger.
Did you ever think you’d see Herm Edwards go for two points?  Thank God he is truly being converted.  Remember when all he talked about was “THE defense”.
And do you all remember last week when Thigpen scored a touchdown, as a receiver?
Pretty soon, ol’ Herm will start acting like a real head coach, not just an entitled defensive coordinator. Watch for the pundits to start counting the one and two point losses, as Chiefs’ win!
Enough about the Chiefs.

At Paul Booker’s house, we talked about volunteering.  Most of us, except Dr. Allen and Bubba Cleaver, are either retired, virtually retired, or just plain tired.  Thus, it didn’t take long before the acts of volunteering replaced the conversation about the poor-played Monday Night football game.  So, while we look ahead to the home-game with New Orleans, we will sprinkle in a few words  about what to do/not to do in retirement.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN:   Charles is still managing and owning a well-established, patient-oriented dental practice.  Somehow, he has eliminated the fear that most people associate with dentists.  He is gentle, painless, and teaches his patients about good dental hygiene and prevention. . . Charles is “befuddled” by it all, especially the play of the Chiefs. . . CHIEFS BY 3.

PAUL BOOKER:  Paul teaches math each summer at Freedom School.  In his working years, Paul was a solid resource for children in the Kansas City, Mo., School District.  His wife, Carolyn, was one of the founding administrators for the local Freedom School movement, along with Dwayne Crompton. . . Turn Out The Lights on the Chiefs. . . NEW ORLEANS BY 7.

CARL CLARK:  Carl says he has “no problem” as a retiree. . .Carl is one of the fortunate ones, having retired from Colgate with a good retirement plan. . . When he is not guarding the children near the schools, he is doing something positive for the Ivanhoe Club and at times, with the Kiwanis. . .The Chiefs will find another way to self-destruct...that’s why he is picking  NEW ORLEANS BY 7.

BUBBA CLEAVER:  Just won his third term as a U.S. Congressman by a landslide.. . . Everyone should see him interact with his grandchildren. . . Cleaver has no plans or room for retirement. . . People are talking again about Presidential appointments. . . Not likely. . .He can’t talk any more about the Chiefs. . . NEW ORLEANS BY 10.

IKE GARDNER:  Ike is succinct about his volunteering.  He candidly reflects that he worked two jobs for his family and he ain’t doing nothing else, period.  However, his lovely wife, Lura, Veterans Administration Hospital retiree, continues to volunteer at the City Union Mission. . . Ike does acknowledge and welcome the “new Chiefs” and stated the they are “on the way but haven’t quite arrived yet”. . . but not enough to pick the Chiefs this week. . .NEW ORLEANS BY 10

LLOYD GREENFIELD:   Lloyd looks out for the cultural opportunities for his entire community. . . In fact, the Monday Niters will be his guest at the production of “Brewster’s Place” in early December. . . a pearl of a guy...but is not very nice when it comes to the Chiefs. . . Says the Chiefs can’t play 60 minutes of football. . . thus, NEW ORLEANS BY 5

OLLIE HUBBARD:  No doubt about it, Lincoln University is high on Ollie’s list. . . Recently, he sold more tickets than anybody at the recent Lincoln fundraiser. . . Hounds you at 5:30 a.m. . . Also has high hopes for Obama. . . and now he is liking the Chiefs a little bit. . . CHIEFS BY 3

JIM NUNNELLY:  Not quite retired but in the Social Security line. . . has volunteered substantial time to over 50 organizations. . . will spend his retirement launching a consultant business, called “Temporary Executive Services”. . . doesn’t think the Chiefs are temporary. . .CHIEFS BY 7.

ED WEST:  Ed got over with his retirement from AT and T. . . Ed is not exactly lazy but spends a lot of time, repairing and setting up computers for Kansas City home-owners. . .loves his wife, Celeste....she volunteers for senior citizens. . .a likeable family. . .but they don’t like the Chiefs. . . Ed says “they CAN’T beat the SAINTS”. . .NEW ORLEANS BY 6
