paragraphs.text: The winning ways of the Chiefs are gone forever....like home-made pies, real mashed potatoes, pan-fried chicken, John Agnos pig-ear sandwiches, the Birdland, 20-mens Club, Frank’s Place etc.  While we may be melancholy about them, they are not coming back.  Our grandchildren will just have to take our word for it.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN:  Possesses a surreal optimism about the Chiefs. . ..his grandson Robert is a free safety at Grandview Middle...Robert has been with Charles and Beverly since he was 14 months old.believes Kansas City will beat Denver by 14. (Wake up Dr. Allen, have you been to the 6902?)

PAUL BOOKER:  Probably the least controversial of all the Monday Nite Footballers...pleasant style. . . serves a buffet of fine choices...brags all the time about his granddaughter Ashley, who is starting point guard at Penn Valley. . .thinks Denver will show no mercy, Sunday...Denver by 14.

CARL CLARK:  Has the distinction of having both his grandchildren named in his honor, Carl III and Carlynn. . . owns a slick Corvette. . . just elected chairman of the 6902 Board of Directors. . . believes the Chiefs will not win another game...Denver by14.

BUBBA CLEAVER:  will present at the national Congressional Black Caucus on foreclosures. . . talks often to his grandchildren by phone. . . they don’t care about his community standing. . . has over a thousand eight-track tapes. . . nicknamed the stadium Arrowhead United Methodist Church. . . thinks the Chiefs are a cinch to lose again.  Bubba will leave on Sunday to visit the Missouri National Guard troops in Kosovo, Yugoslavia. Denver by 14

IKE GARDNER:  Once put a “no visitors” sign on his hospital-room door...has the personality of an injured wolverine. . . once volunteered for his teacher-daughter Tia. . . takes his nine-year-old grandson Isaiah to 35 Chiefs football games. . . the only dog he ever owned ran away, seeking asylum at Wayside Waifs. . . will have a BIG Birthday on September 26. . . believes the Chiefs are no opposition for Denver...Broncos by 35.

LLOYD GREENFIELD: Is responsible for assuring that all Monday Niters receive an annual dose of culture by arranging to attend a play in the area. . . is new in the “grandfather” role for his seven-month-old granddaughter, Geneva. . . wants to provide her with a good foundation because he never had one. . . is considering wearing a toupee. . . bald or not, believes Chiefs have too many internal problems to win. . . Denver by 14 1/2.

OLLIE HUBBARD:  Is one of the best fish-cooks in the Kansas City area. . .has cooked many a fish and made a lot of chili raising funds for Lincoln University . . . rescued his now wife from one of the largest cities in Missouri, Macon. . . has more out of town visitors than the entire hotel industry. . . loves to go to Mount Pleasant, Texas. . . believes the Broncos will kill the Chiefs. Denver by 35.

JIM NUNNELLY:  All four of his grandchildren are named in his honor....grandson Chris now attending Missouri Western at St. Joseph. . .hails from Columbia, Missouri. . .featured in Ebony magazine in 1975. . .can be seen at Gates, Niecies, Peachtree, M and M Bakery all the time. . . wife, Janice never cooks. . . will one day write a book about these Monday Nite Footballers. . .moans for the “good ol’ days”. . .they are never coming back. . .no Dante Hall, no victory...Denver by 28.

ED WEST: Has two adolescent granddaughters in California. . .son Damon was the music producer for “Dreamgirls”. . . had a strong influence on his son’s career by enrolling him in Christian School. . ..can fix anything electronic. . . was the audio engineer at St. James. . . wife, Celeste is an advocate for alternative school students. . . believes the defense will be Cutlerized. Denver by 20.

Denver by 35.JIM NUNNELLY:  All four of his grandchildren are named in his honor....grandson Chris now attending Missouri Western at St. Joseph. . .hails from Columbia, Missouri. . .featured in Ebony magazine in 1975. . .can be seen at Gates, Niecies, Peachtree, M and M Bakery all the time. . . wife, Janice never cooks. . . will one day write a book about these Monday Nite Footballers. . .moans for the “good ol’ days”. . .they are never coming back. . .no Dante Hall, no victory...Denver by 28.ED WEST: Has two adolescent granddaughters in California. . .son Damon was the music producer for “Dreamgirls”. . . had a strong influence on his son’s career by enrolling him in Christian School. . ..can fix anything electronic. . . was the audio engineer at St. James. . . wife, Celeste is an advocate for alternative school students. . . believes the defense will be Cutlerized. Denver by 20.

Carl “The Quiet One” Clark
I have been a season ticket holder for the Chiefs since 1963.  I’ve seen some good years and some not-so-good seasons.

But, this year is the very worst team the Chiefs have ever fielded.  And because of that, I believe the Chiefs will not win a single game in 2009.  The offensive line is poor.  The play calling is poor. And the coach is trying to hold too many positions.  And on top of that, Haley needs to “bawl himself out” every now and then for his participation in the Chiefs’ demise.

On a positive note, the only thing that the Chiefs do well is their kicking game. But the weak offensive line, the overpaid and under-delivering quarterback and the poor coaching will continue.  That spells more losses and long season.  Everyone will beat the hell out of the Chiefs.

I’m taking my second pill
Paul Booker     New York by a lot
A Giant killer, KC is not
Carl Clark     New York by 14
Giants will climb the Chiefs’ beanstalk!
Bubba Cleaver      New York by 15
Chiefs have a GIANT problem
Ike Gardner     New York by 28
Chiefs should play the Midgets, not the Giants
Lloyd Greenfield     New York by 12
Chiefs have a long way to go.
Ollie Hubbard     New York by 25
Not gonna win another game!
Jim Nunnelly    Kansas City by 3
Eli fails!
Ed West      New York by 20
Manning will have a record-setting day
Eric L. Wesson      New York by 24
Any game against the Chiefs is an automatic win and a record offensive and defensive day!

paragraphs.text: Peanute Brittle, Melody Lanes And The Chiefs

frames.text: Peanute Brittle, Melody Lanes And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: We, Monday Niters, have given up on the Chiefs.
They have been beaten badly by the doormats of the NFL, i.e. Buffalo and Detroit.
What’s more they have lost their only offensive hope through injury. . .Jamal Charles. All they have left now is Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel.

Yes, that’s an appropriate name for Cassel because he is worth only “peanuts” and he is always injured, therefore, “brittle”. So, he is now a  bona fide member of a long line of “broken” Chiefs’ quarterbacks.
So, we collectively think the Chiefs will get shocked again Sunday by the San Diego Chargers. The Chargers will strike the Chiefs for with six or seven touchdowns.

Speaking of strikes, we talked a lot about old bowling alleys and good bowling athletes. There have been several bowling establishments frequented by African Americans in the ‘60s -- Monarch Lanes, Melody Lanes, King Louie East and even K.C. Bowl in Kansas. And of late, there is a major bowling contingency that now goes to Premier out in Raytown. Just go out there on a Tuesday afternoon and see scores of seniors rolling the ball. And on Fridays and Thursdays, you can find some of the best bowling around. So, in this column, we prefer to talk about bowlers of yesteryears, rather than talk about Peanut Brittle And The Candy Stripers.
So now for a walk down Memory Lanes.

Dr. Charles Allen: Way back in 1952, Doc was a pin-setter at Sakin’s bowling alley, near Linwood and Troost. In the old days, bowling pins were set manually, and usually by African American youth at white establishments. Though he did not bowl much, he felt unsafe in that job. But not unsafe about the locals. Chiefs by 3

Paul “6902” Booker: Booker believes the there is no way that the Chiefs can beat San Diego. And he has felt that way since he came here in 1966. He does remember Fred Broski’s bowling for dollars. Money or not. San Diego by 40

Carl “Classy” Clark: Believes the Chiefs are just pitiful. But does remember being a league bowler at Melody Lanes in 1965, on a team sponsored by Northwestern Mutual Insurance Company. Not enough insurance for the Chiefs to win, though.  San Diego by 14

Congressman “Bubba” Cleaver: Believes the Chiefs are “out of and out for the season. Wisely, Cleaver has appointed a group to research and honor the black bowlers of the past. This group includes Jauqua Preston, Joe Newsome, Nero Hartridge, Ron Winfrey, Maxine Walker, LaDonna Hendrix, Sam Coleman, Jiles Dunn, Deborah Cheadle Thomas, Joycelyn Burgo, Alex Harris, Willie Henderson Jim Nunnelly and Bill Johnson. An announcement is expected soon on the outcomes. Outcome bad for Chiefs. San Diego by 10

Ike “Spoiled by Niecie’s” Gardner: Ike was pin-setter at a white bowling alley in the ‘50s. As a worker, he had to use the back door to enter. Now, that was a long time ago.  He hated segregation as much as he hates the Chiefs.  San Diego by 35

Lloyd “Loyal Up To A Point” Greenfield: Lloyd is one of the seniors who bowl at Premier on Tuesdays. Bowling a cool 152 average, he is surrounded by seniors who can really bowl and who know a lot about Kansas City’s history. But, this time, Lloyd switches over from the Chiefs. San Diego by 7

Ollie “Breaking New ” Hubbard: Ollie remembers going to parties at the Rhythm Lanes on Troost, way back in the sixties. The teenagers went there for music and refreshments. But, the Chiefs are not refreshing at all and he expects a bolt of lightning to hit the Chiefs. San Diego by 35

Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly: started bowling at King Louie East, when Ron Winfrey became the first black to manage a bowling establishment. Hopes to record some of this rich bowling history. But history will be made Sunday when the Charges run up the largest score in NFL history on the Chiefs. San Diego by 50

Ed “Still Mentoring” West: Being brought up in Osawatamie, Kansas, Ed was only permitted to bowl one night a week at the white bowling alley. However, later he joined the St. James bowling league in 1980. Never a true bowler, he feels the Chiefs have no coach, no offense, no defense thus no win. San Diego by 38

paragraphs.text: By Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly
Well, we all know that the Chiefs are still losing.  But, so is Oakland, the Chiefs’ next Arrowhead opponent.
And, we all know about the 40 year rivalry between the two teams.  And we also know that, at one time, these AFC stalwarts were competitive and even Super Bowl entrants.

But, like a lot of things, each of these two historical giants have fallen on “hard times”.  Neither is expected to do much at all, in 2008.  Like last year and the year before that.  In fact, these conference siblings are in a shaky state of re-building i.e. they will lose every game they play.

Thus, the game out at Arrowhead  will be “a battle of the behinders”.  To mark such a sad occasion, I have changed the names of the teams, to reflect how even they are. . . in their likelihood to lose. From now on, these  two teams are called the Kansas City Raiders and the Oakland Chiefs.  That’s because they are both losers and they will continue doing “hard times of 2008”.
Enough said.  Allow me tell you a little about each one of the Monday Nite Footballers Group. . . one by one. . . with their predictions for Sunday.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN (Kansas City) -- A dentist by profession. . . known for his painless procedures and his professional office staff. . a Kappa by fraternity.... an extraordinary grandfather. . . believes Kansas City will win by touchdown because the Chiefs will play better at home.

PAUL BOOKER..(Oakland). . . retired educator...was a specialist in assisting needy students...hails from the Bootheel. . . watches ESPN everyday...good with figures...self-appointed liquor inspector...fantastic grandfather. . . believes Oakland will win by 10 because of the pitiful Chiefs’ pitiful offensive line.

CARL CLARK (Kansas City). . . retired journeyman at Colgate...car enthusiast. world traveler...socially aware and respected. . . effective grandfather....daily visitor to 69th and Prospect. . . believes Kansas City will win by a touchdown, even though neither team is worthy of winning.

BUBBA CLEAVER.(Kansas City). . . nationally-acclaimed elected official and minister. . . former Mayor and now United States Congressman. . .studious and thoughtful to a fault.. . . can remember thousands of people and their exact conversations. . . a proud grandfather. . . believes Kansas City will win by 10 because the Oakland Raiders don’t  “raid” any more.

IKE GARDNER..(Oakland). . . fearless pragmatist. . . attends St. James and sits near the back on the aisle. . .a steadfast grandfather. . . cantankerous as hell. . . has seats on the 50 yard line at Arrowhead. . . was a key player in the early days of desegregation of schools. . .believes Kansas City by 3 because there is no chance for Oakland to win.

LLOYD GREENFIELD (Kansas City). . . a retired firefighter  turned real estate enthusiast. . . owns hundreds of model cars...has a motorcycle. . . has starred in many theatrical events. . . clear-headed and respected. . . stays in contact with his old high school class..believes the Chiefs will win by 3 but it will be on a “wing and a prayer”.

OLLIE HUBBARD (Oakland). . . Loves and is married to Lincoln university. . . been known to lie about everything. . . knows everybody in Kansas City...formerly a vice principal, now retired....loves to prepare food for his friends so that he can eat the most.....a remarkable grandfather....thinks the Kansas City-Oakland game will be a toss-up but Chiefs could win by 14.

JIM NUNNELLY..(Kansas City). . .has consulted with over 200 organizations nationwide....instrumental in building anddeveloping the Rodgers Health Center. . . .a relentless advocate for teenagers. . . a complete grandfather.......works at Jackson County. . . believes the Chiefs and the Raiders are the two worst teams in the NFL but come Sunday, the Chiefs will deploy a “Midwest Coast Defense” and win by 3.

ED WEST....(Kansas City). . . a gadgetician. . . can construct or repair any computer...has a huge big screen tv. . .a substitute teacher in Raytown....was All-America at Pittsburg State. . .devout member of St. James. . . an encouraging grandfather...believes Kansas City will win by a touchdown because he “just a Raider-hater”

frames.text: Monday Nighters

paragraphs.text: It’s Friday and we are still gloating over the Chiefs victory over Denver, last Sunday.  It seems like it was a dream and soon we will all wake up to reality. . . that the Chiefs will return to their losing ways, this Sunday against Carolina.  Most of the guys felt like Carolina will topple the Chiefs and Herm Edwards will return to his confusing testimony about the plight of the 2008 Chiefs.

By the way, did you notice how ol” Herm hugged Larry Johnson after the last Kansas City touchdown.  He whispered in Larry’s ear “thanks for saving my job, man”.  And then later, Carl Peterson came out of his suite and said essentially the same...”you gave me one more year, LJ..I apologize for putting you on the bench”.

No doubt about it LJ saved the day for these two.  Already the St. Louis Rams have fired their coach.  And guess who is next if we don’t play well against Carolina?  But last Monday night, we spent most of our time talking about the how our old-time teachers influenced us.  Thus, we remembered them.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN:  Thinks the Kansas City School District suffers from negative press. . . thanks his former teacher, Luke Ponder for clearing the path for him to attend college on an acting scholarship. . . acting or not, Charles thinks the Chiefs are in a winning mode..Chiefs by 7
PAUL BOOKER:  Sometimes called the Apostle Paul. . .Thinks that more parental involvement is needed. . . believes the Carolina moon will not shine on the Chiefs...Carolina by 13.

CARL CLARK:  Is a proponent of teachers taking tests for certification. . . is a stickler for accountability. . . in or out of trouble, begs the Chiefs not to get too happy because they are still losers. . . Carolina by 14

IKE GARDNER:  Grandson Isaiah often sings at St. James...says that when kids are going to private schools, they are saying that education is a valued asset. . . likes Christmas but believes Santa only comes once a year for the Chiefs...Carolina by 17
LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Feels the teaching curriculum needs to be upgraded...and teachers ought to go back to basics in education. . . .thinks the Chiefs can lose all the games...Carolina by 7.

JIM NUNNELLY:  Favorite teacher was the school secretary, Beulah Ralph, who taught him about school administration...took time with him...believes principals needs executive coaching to achieve goals. . . .corporate or not, the Chiefs will win their second game in a row because the defense will give Larry Johnson more opportunities. . .Chiefs by 10

ED WEST:  Feels the Chiefs will start another losing streak against Carolina. . . feels that teachers pre-judge most black kids without really knowing their assets. . . Chiefs won’t overcome losing label. . . Carolina by 14.

OLLIE HUBBARD:  Need to increase the amount of homework, especially in math and reading. . . homework is instruction hours and they help out in test scores. . . parents must help. . . last week, the Chiefs made it sooooo goooooood, let’s keep it up. . . Chiefs by 14

BUBBA CLEAVER:  In Washington this, dealing with the bailout. . . voted against first package because it did not contain enough provisions to help everyday people.. . . is actively campaigning on behalf of Obama. . . thinks the Chiefs’ win over Denver was a fluke. . . thus, Carolina by 10.

paragraphs.text: Every time, we go to Ed West’s house, the sparks fly.
First on our list was to compliment the Chiefs on a good effort.
Enough said.
Instead, we talked about who should be fired in the Chiefs’ front office.

But, then we began to predict if Barack Obama would actual win the highest elective office in our nation.  Here’s a summary of the discussions from some of the most opinionated, talkative, and knowledgeable guys in Kansas City.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN: He thinks the whole coaching squad ought to be sacked, especially Günther Cunningham and Carl Peterson, the Chiefs’ General Manager and President.. . .Charles is “guardedly optimistic” about Obama’s chances to become President of the United States. . . still thinks the Chiefs will win at Arrowhead. . . Chiefs by 3

CARL CLARK: He, too, thinks Günther is the problem with the Chiefs and must be the first to go. . .Unlike Booker, Carl thinks Obama will win but by a very small margin. . . he has no doubts as to who will win Sunday. . . Tampa Bay by 14.

BUBBA CLEAVER: Unlike the rest of us, feels that the problem is not only in the coaching ranks. . . he thinks it is Larry Johnson who is the disruptive force on the Chiefs. . . In the same line of reasoning, Cleaver believes that Obama will win by a small margin. . . Believes Warren Dunn will do what he has “done” to other teams. . . run them raggedy..Tampa Bay by 10.

IKE GARDNER:  Ike was rather nice on Monday night, he only called Carl Clark out of his name only once. . . He hopes Obama will win but was quick to remind everyone that elections can be stolen and referred us back to the Gore-Bush crap in Florida. . . He thinks the Buccaneers will find their pot of gold at Arrowhead Sunday. . . Tampa Bay by 21.

He feels that it will be a long night because of the long voting lines and there will be procedural issues for several days. . . but in the end, Obama will be our next President of the United States. . . He has not given up on the Chiefs...Chiefs by 6.

paragraphs.text: Man, it was so hard to talk about the Kansas City Chiefs in serious manner.
In fact, Ed West recognized that the Chiefs played better.  And Carl Clark and Ike Gardner actually praised Thigpen, the last of the rotating Chiefs’ quarterbacks.

The Tennessee Titans (8-0) are for real as the only undefeated team in the NFL.  Worth noting is that the AFC West is the weakest conference in the NFL, having no team with a winning record.  What’s more is that our Chiefs have the worst record in the worst division.

Now, what a distinction!  Well, we then turned our attention to hoping that (Barack) Obama will become the next President of the United States.  We, as African Americans, will no longer have a color-fence to hide behind.  We can savor and elongate this important event, by achieving unprecedented excellence in everything we attempt.
With that, here are our predictions for the next week.
Dr. Charles Allen. . . He’s speechless behind these Chiefs. . . Charles always votes for the Chiefs. . . even though most of us believe he is loyal to a fault. . . Chiefs by 3
Paul Booker. . . He thinks L.T., San Diego’s running back, will run up and down the field on the Chiefs. . . Chargers by 13
Carl Clark. . . attended Mary Helen Parker’s surprise birthday party last week. . .he thinks the Chiefs cannot survive another attack. . . Chargers by 7
Bubba Cleaver. . . is campaigning hard for Obama. . .is being helpful for those faced with foreclosure issues...did foreclose on the Chiefs. . . San Diego by 10

Ike Gardner. . . Ike is kinda subdued these days. . . he is nicer than he has ever been. . . not sure what’s up...but he still knows the Chiefs cannot win. . . and believes they will find another way to lose. . . Chargers by 21
Lloyd Greenfield. . . Loyal Lloyd is being loyal again...he believes if the Chiefs try, he will try to support them...Chargers by 3
Ollie Hubbard. . . wife, Sandra and he have been helpful to planning community events, especially for Lincoln university. . . not that supportive of the Chiefs. . . Chargers by 30

Jim Nunnelly. . . His mind is stayed on Obama. . . thanks everyone who engineered his retirement party, where 350 persons attended last Friday. . . he doesn’t believe the Chiefs are retired, quite yet. Look for Smith, Charles and Bowe to show out. . . Chiefs by 3
Ed West. . . A staunch Obama supporter. . . an avid Cleaver fan. . . but not Herm Edwards...thinks Herm has too many rookies out there and lightning will again strike them. . . Chargers by 20

paragraphs.text: The Chiefs suck.
End of conversation.

Fortunately, the Monday Niters talk about more than the vicissitudes of this so-called professional football team. Out at Dr. Allen’s house, amid the Greek-influenced, romaine-based salad and another Greek concoction, man we talked about old remedies, used by our folks in the thirties and forties.  And we focused our attention on some special senior citizens, those that are permanently imprinted in our memories.

Congressman Cleaver called from Washington to share some news about the over-demanded/under-supplied inaugural tickets. So, instead of beating some “dead Chiefs”, let’s look in on a not-so-typical Monday Niter word-fest.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN:  Charles is sending Mrs. Mila Banks a special, belated Birthday wish.  She believes the Chiefs will eventually develop into a fine team.  That’s just like Charles, going out and recruiting people who still think the Chiefs can win. Mila says that the Monday Niters are “. . .men of little faith”.  Right you are! But Charles isn’t. . . CHIEFS BY; 3

PAUL BOOKER:  Booker is usually a nice guy, except when it comes to the Chiefs.  Then, he turns into this “killer monster”, thinking that the Chiefs have no offense at all.  He did smile when he acknowledged the wisdom and faith of his 84-year-old sister from Hayti, Missouri.  This lady bore and reared thirteen children, in her lifetime.  Booker says his mom used the yellow of an egg to reduce the swelling, caused by Mumps.  Okkkkkkk! Anyway, BUFFALO BY 13

CARL CLARK: Carl claimed that his folks cured him of pneumonia by using skunk oil and honey.  That one doesn’t pass the smell test.  Carl mentioned seeing Mila Banks around town, especially at social events like Ivanhoe and Twin City functions.  “She always talks about the Chiefs”, said Carl smiling.  Smile or no smile. Smell or no smell.  The Chiefs will be stampeded Sunday. . .BUFFALO BY 14

BUBBA CLEAVER:  Cleaver is stuck in Washington, fighting for the bailout of the automakers.  He says he cannot vote any other way because 2,000 or more jobs will be lost here in Kansas City, if he doesn’t support the bailout.  Cleaver called the Monday Niters and told them he is being besieged with inaugural ticket requests.  He is planning a lottery to address the thousands of requests...In the meantime, he thinks the Chiefs still have not found a way to win. . . BUFFALO BY 14.

IKE GARDNER:  Ike believes the Chiefs are going to get a steady diet of Buffalo chips, Sunday.  Ike has lost friends because of his no-patience position with the Chiefs.  But he did smile when he spoke of Mila Banks.  He remembers her as a great teacher at R.T. Coles.  Ike even congratulated Mila for being such a fearless disciplinarian, something sorely needed in today’s schools. During the discussion about home remedies, Ike came up with something called “juniper tar and sugar” for colds.  Will this work for the Chiefs?  Apparently not. . .  BUFFALO BY 13

LLOYD GREENFIELD:  Lloyd said there was something called “666” for colds.  Is this some kind of devil reference?  And Lloyd chimed in about Mila Banks being at a recent Ivanhoe party.  Lloyd reminded Mila that he was one of her late husband’s “jelly beans” (a term used frequently for students by Isaiah Banks).  Speaking of jelly beans, Lloyd thinks that the Chiefs can’t even beat a piece of candy.  BUFFALO BY 10

OLLIE HUBBARD  Ollie talks with Mila Banks often, to check on her.  Ollie said Mila and her friends went down to visit Carl Connor in Columbia recently.  Growing up on 27th and Olive, Ollie says his mother gave him turpentine and sugar for colds.  If the cold got real bad, she would apply “goose grease” all over his huge body. But, nothing can help these Chiefs with a win.  Look for number 10 loss, Sunday. . . BUFFALO BY 20

JIM NUNNELLY:  He brought up  Carl Connor, who now resides in Columbia, Mo., near his nephew, Charles Allen.   Connor reads this column religiously, even though he is at least ninety five.  He is alert and like Mila, taught here in the Kansas City, Mo., School District for years.  Carl is and has always been a Missouri Tiger sports fan.  That’s good news because the Chiefs sure ain’t doing much. In Columbia, the old folks thought Vick’s saffe would cure colds, pneumonia, hangovers. . .everything.  But, it can’t help the Chiefs BUFFALO BY 30

ED WEST:  Ed is from rural Kansas and like all rural families, they relied on certain remedies for survival.  His family consumed a lot of iron supplement, called 3-S Tonic.  It must have helped because Ed is a picture of health and still uses “Three S” everyday.  It seems that the Chiefs are taking something these days for they are definitely improving.  But, according to Ed, not enough.  BUFFALO BY 10.

paragraphs.text: Amid all the opulent commercials, the teams on the field were not expected to be in Tampa Sunday.  Oh yea, all of you AFC fans ere thinking that New England would rise again.
And those New Yorkers thought that the Giants would represent the NFC and return to the most luxurious Sunday of the year.

And some of you thought that Tony Dungy would re-take his Colts, before he retired with his best-selling book proceeds. Well, we were all wrong and we now have (Mike) Tomlin and the Steelers versus Kurt Warner and the Cardinals. And the only thing they have in common is that neither was supposed to be in Super Bowl 43.
Pittsburgh, under its black, second-year coach, has come to be known for its awesome defense. And according to Cleaver, Ike, Carl, and Lloyd, Pittsburgh will slaughter Arizona.

But, some of us will remember Kurt Warner, who conducted the “Greatest Show On Turf”.  He was the pass-happy quarterback under the (Dick) Vermeil-led St. Louis Rams (who went on to the Super Bowl).  So it will an “Arm and Hammer” game that will keep us glued to our big screens, at least until the multi-million-dollar commercials begin.

Laugh of the Day:  Chiefs will be in Super Bowl 44, after going undefeated in 2009. And Carl Peterson will be the General Manager of the opposing NFC team and guess who will be the Head Coach?.. Ha Ha Ha!
Charles Allen: Pittsburgh by 14.    Experience, experience, experience!
Paul Booker:   Pittsburgh by 14.    I’m black and biased...Tomlin goes all the way!
Carl Clark:    Pittsburgh by 7.     Defense will win this game!
Bubba Cleaver:  Pittsburgh by 14.    Arizona is the biggest fluke in NFL history!
Ike Gardner:  Pittsburgh by 7.     Too much defense!
Lloyd Greenfield: Pittsburgh by 7.     Steelers will steal it!
Ollie Hubbard:  Pittsburgh by 7.     Ain’t no mountain high enough!
Ed West:     Pittsburgh by 10.    Remember, I went to Pittsburgh.
Tracy Allen: Pittsburgh by 7. Steeler’s “steel” will contain Fitzgerald, Warner
Eric Wesson:   Pittsburgh by 17.   It is a great time to be black in America!
Donna Stewart (publisher):  Arizona by 7.

paragraphs.text: Despite the ill wishes of the diehard “Manning maniacs”, the New Orleans Saints did go marching in..they crucified the Colts, this past Sunday at the Super Bowl.  In fact, it is hard to find anyone who was “for” the Colts, after that second display of  second half redemption. No one will ever forget the score at the end of the first half...neither will we ever forget the going for the Saints’ gutsy playcalling, even though they failed to score...and no one will forget the on-side kick that split the “Red Sea” for the Saints...and God Almighty blessed little Tracy Porter with a “Manning bullet” and the rest is history.  Good going Saints....you made it all worth watching.  Now back to those who predicted the games.  Here are the Saints and here are the Ponies.
THOSE WHO THOUGHT THE SAINTS WOULD WIN!

Vicki Frazier, Renee Gardner, Breana Jordan, Montoya Lucas, Kosha Johnson, Danielle Morris, Rich McCauley, Jim “Grand Dad” Nunnelly, Erica Nunnelly, Jazel Nunnelly, Christian Nunnelly, Gerald Pegg, LaMetria Pegg, Margo Quiriconi, Eric L. Wesson, Arionne Williams and Patricia Wright.
THOSE WHO NEW THE SAINTS WOULD WIN!
Eric L. Wesson
THOSE WHO
MISTAKENLY
PICKED THE COLTS
TO WIN!

Dr. Charles Allen, Paul Booker, CB Cadenhead, Carl Clark,Congressman Cleaver, Dyan Deveraux, Charles Fort (San Diego), Ike “Papaw” Gardner, Lloyd Greenfield, Ollie Hubbard, Clyde McQueen (Full Employment Council), Donna Stewart, and Ed West,

FINAL WORDS!  We will not remind you that it has been a long time coming for the Saints.  Just about the same time it has been since the Chiefs have been to the Super Bowl.  Every team in the AFC West has been since we last went in 1970.  Let’s hope and pray our Chiefs make the right draft choices and make it easier for Kansas City to compete.  And of course, we, Monday Niters along with THE CALL, are doing our part to get Otis Taylor into the NFL Hall Of Fame....now that would be something....and to the Colts’ fans...maybe next year.  For now, the rest of us will gloat over the fact that WE were in “that number”....when the Saints went marching in....

paragraphs.text: No one knows what these Chiefs are going to do this season.  Everyone is so righteously caught up in the training camp move to St. Joseph, as if where a team practices wins football games.  Nah, it ain’t happening.  It still counts what happens on the field, starting the second week in September.  But, we Monday Niters are admittedly getting swooped up by the hype.

As the guys gather every Friday at a local club, the Chiefs and the 2010 season dominates the discussion.  Of course, the oldies but goodies music helps them reminisce about the good old days, when the Chiefs really were Chiefs. . . not Chefs.  But here is some of the pre-season chatter going on at 69th and Prospect.
TRIVIA QUESTION FOR THE WEEK: What teams played in the last Super Bowl?

1) Ed West is steadily teaching his fellow Monday Niters about technology.  Armed with a i-phone, Ed is able to respond quickly to any football question that needs a quick answer.  Where there once was arguments, now it is a simple...talk-into-the-phone and within a few seconds, there is a bona fide answer.  He also got Carl to buy one of those nifty phones.  And Ike even bought a laptop.  So did Nunnelly.  And Booker is actually going to Best Buy every week to look at one.

2)  All the talk this week is about the upcoming weekend Hall of Fame game.  You know the great Jerry Rice, Emmitt Smith and Floyd Little are being inducted into the NFL Hall of Fame. What else can be said about Jerry Rice that hasn’t been said?  That is a heck of a thing..that Hall of Fame in Canton, Ohio.  Carl Clark, Dr. Charles Allen, Lloyd Greenfield, and Ike Gardner have attended ceremonies there in years past.  They recommend it for everyone.

By the way, Floyd Little wore number 44, just like Jim Brown at Syracuse.  He was a Pro-Bowler for five years, while in Denver.  Those were the days when the Broncos were the doormat of the AFC.  He waited 30 years to get to the Hall of Fame.  Good things do come to those who wait.

3)  This week’s Hall of Fame game is between the Cincinnati Bengals and the Dallas Cowboys.  You might just see Romo hook up with TO.  Maybe. And for sure, you will see whether Ocho Cinco still has it.  Probably not.  That game is Sunday night.

4) Been up to St. Joseph to the Chiefs’ training camp?  If you go, pay for your parking. Do not take the “free parking” option.  You will walk for miles, getting to the state-of-the-art training facilities.  You will be moved by the university’s football field, as well as the Chief’s new digs.  Matter of fact, the Chiefs’ store is in a tent, designed for you to visit....whether you want to or not.  And given the heat, any additional walking is not good.  Remember, take the paying parking.  Or else you will be sorry.

ANSWER TO THE TRIVIA QUESTION:  Well, we know it wasn’t the Chiefs.  But, it was New Orleans Saints and the Indianapolis Colts.  The Saints beat the Favre-led Vikings and the Colts beat the Jets to get to the big game.  By the way, look for the Colts to make Peyton Manning the highest paid football player ever.  He is one of the few quarterbacks who has started every game since joining the NFL.  Big, big bucks are on the way, Peyton.

PAUL “THE APOSTLE” BOOKER
It appears to be another bummer of a year for the Kansas City Chiefs.

And while we often blame the players, the coaches, particularly the Head Coach, should bear a lot of the criticisms, as well. Todd Haley is new, never having been a head coach before.  Yet, he treats his players with so little respect.  He appears disgruntled and mad, at all times.
Doesn’t he know that he is dealing with men, not children?

That motivation and praise is still the most effective aspect of leadership? That a pat on the back is what this young talented team needs?  If he continues the risky “my way or the highway” approach, the Chiefs will again be among the biggest losers.

A bitter pill to swallow
Paul Booker     Eagles by 14

Carl Clark         Eagles by 14
Eagles soar over KC
Bubba Cleaver     Eagles by 14
Chiefs are not ready, regardless of McNabb status

Eagles show no brotherly love, even w/o McNabb

The recession is everywhere

Hustle pays off

Johnson and Johnson set records

Haley’s comets can’t get off ground

Eagles will find a way to lose

Every underdog has its day

paragraphs.text: Editor, THE CALL:
Each week during football season, I look forward to reading the “Monday Niters” predictions and the commentary by Jim “Granddad” Nunnelly.
Mr. Nunnelly’s commentary in a recent “CALL” issue was particularly interesting as he told a little about each man in the “Monday Nite Footballers group.”
Nunnelly is an excellent writer. He knows how to make words on a page come alive.
Even though the “Monday Niters” lead varied lives with different professions, they enjoy commonalities that make them a cohesive group of remarkable black men.

In a recent  write-up, Nunnelly described these grandfathers of the group from Allen to West as: extraordinary, fantastic, effective, proud, steadfast, remarkable, complete, and encouraging. For what more could one ask?
Monday Niters, “Keep on keeping on.” BRAVO!!.
Terry Strother
Burlington, Iowa

paragraphs.text: For the most part, we again ignored the awful plight of the Kansas City Chiefs, this past Monday.  We were entertained at Ike’s house, out in Raytown.  Ike claims he fixed the red beans and rice, laced with gumbo-like polish sausages and topped with onions.  His family came to his rescue, with Lura, Shelley and Roosevelt providing various levels of hospitality.  And the Chiefs, on a bye week, did not provide much conversational opportunities.  Thus, the conversation drifted into lots of words about Lincoln University’s Homecoming weekend. Being alumni, several of our members attended the long-weekend and were greeted with the Temptations and a great half-time show, at the football game.  Of particular note was the maturing Lincoln University Marching Band.  Ollie Gates, favorite of old’ L.U., made his annual trek to Jefferson City, parked his motor-home on the football field, and provided Lincoln’s President with his annual donation.

But, Lincoln has changed dramatically, since the days of segregation.  In fact, Lincoln is quite diverse, with many drive-in, day students having enrolled since the early seventies.  That’s why it is referred to as an “historically black college and university”. So while the Chiefs will get slaughtered at Arrowhead Sunday, much of the conversation, for us, concentrated on an important topic, like Lincoln University. Unlike the Chiefs, Lincoln beat Xavier 56-7.

DR. CHARLES ALLEN  Proud alumni of Lincoln...attended the homecoming ceremonies last week and immediately noticed a major difference, compared to the sixties...there were curfews then, especially for girls...there were no co-ed dorms.. this year, the Homecoming queen, a beautiful black lady, was escorted by a Caucasian guy.....and Charles clearly missed the “foot”, a collection of joints at the bottom of the famous hills...he missed Miss Leona’s famous chili-skillet-stew...she made sure that no Lincoln student ever went hungry....no coming back y’all...but Charles believes that the Chiefs are saying that “a setback is a set-up for a come-back” and predicts CHIEFS BY 7

PAUL BOOKER  Also an alumni from the Bootheel...also misses Miss Leona’s cooking that combined everything into a single dish....Booker ate there twice a day because he hated the campus food...looks forward to meeting all of his old friends at Edna Brannock’s mother’s house each year...liked the Temptations. but coming back from Jefferson City, thought about the Chiefs and just knew that the Titans will Tennessee-waltz the Chiefs...TENNESSEE BY 13.

CARL CLARK  Carl was rather quiet, this past Monday...in fact, he fell into a deep sleep a couple of times....usually talkative but rather subdued....he enjoyed attending Lincoln’s homecoming during his high school days...he didn’t go back after a girl threw some chitterlings on Apple Jack...he hasn’t been back since. someone must have thrown some chitlins on the Chiefs....Carl predicts TENNESSEE BY 14.

IKE GARDNER  Ike’s affiliation with Lincoln arose because he was refused admission to Missouri University and they, then, suggested he enrolled at Lincoln, instead....noted that most black colleges, including Howard where he attended, had curfews based on the day of the week, allowing later times as the week progressed...did not ever attend Lincoln but has been a staunch supporter of HBCU’s...turning to the Chiefs, Ike is not impressed with Chiefs at all...thinks they can’t stop rolling downhill...TENNESSEE BY 25.

LLOYD GREENFIELD  His cousin, Charlene Boswell attended Lincoln university....she was instrumental in organizing the Metropolitan Spiritual church...Lloyd was a sprinter at Lincoln High School way back in the early fifties....is producing a cd, featuring singers Jackie Mackrel and Geneva Price....keeps asking the question...have you ever seen a Tennessean walk....well, TENNESSEE BY 14.

OLLIE HUBBARD  Graduated from Lincoln University in 1966....a major contributor to Lincoln....impressed with the growth of Lincoln over the years...attended “every” homecoming between 1967 and 2005, stopping because of a leg problems...salutes all the Kansas Citians who have attended Lincoln, including Donna Stewart, Ollie Gates, Georgia Buchanan, Bob Wheeler, and Gurnie Gunther...while he still plans to support Lincoln university, he has given up on the Chiefs entirely...TENNESSEE BY 30.

JIM NUNNELLY  He chose to enroll at Missouri University, even though he had a full scholarship to Lincoln....attended several homecomings...as a high school student, won the Armistead Pride Journalism award three years in a row...lived in Columbia and knew many Lincoln alumni, including Erma Monroe, Juanita Dixon, Mary Patton, Joanne Herndon, Emma Turner, George Brooks, Montell Washington....lot of years have left by but not his faith in the Chiefs...CHIEFS BY 3

ED WEST  Believes the Chiefs’ losing streak is about to take off...was a track and football athlete at Pittsburg State...competed in the long jump against Herman Gant...who was a miler at Lincoln.....Gant is still in great shape and walked every day from the Capitol hotel to the Lincoln campus during Lincoln’s Homecoming...like the rest of us, Ed is just plain tired of the Chiefs....TENNESSEE BY 30.

ROOSEVELT SCULARK  Ike’s son-in-law....alumni of Jackson State and Howard, both hbcu’s...interacted with the Monday Niters throughout the evening...clean-cut and credible...believes the Chiefs’ secondary cannot stop anything or anybody...TENNESSEE BY 24...

paragraphs.text: Thank You, Lisa Page

frames.text: Thank You, Lisa Page

paragraphs.text: Surely, every one of our readers have heard the smashing, gospel hit song, “I Just Want To Thank You”.

With that in mind, we, Monday Niters, are in a “Thanksgiving spirit” and want to lace our column with both the song and the season in mind,  Thus, we are asking the question.....what player should the Chiefs be most thankful for.

And then, we are asking each Monday Niter, what he is personally thankful for.  And in between the lines, we will gently place a few facts, along side our prediction of the Seattle-Kansas City game on Sunday.  Actually, after beating Arizona at home last Sunday, the Chiefs, at 6-4, have a better record than the Seahawks, at 5-5.

And like old times, the Chiefs are undefeated at home.  Conversely, except for Cleveland, the Chiefs have lost four games on the road.    Unjustly, the “haters” were not courteous enough to call us and congratulate us “loyalists” on our predictions, last week.  But, the “haters” are like the “tea party folks”, they just want to hate.

Dr. Charles Allen: Doc says the Chiefs ought to be thankful for the maturation and development of Jamaal Charles, their third year running back. And being the gentleman he is, he says he personally is thankful for his fine family, his health, and his many patients, who have placed great faith in his professional capabilities.    Chiefs by 10

Paul Booker: Fresh from celebrating his two birthdays, Booker is thankful that he hasn’t been run out of town for his many disloyal predictions, against the Chiefs.  However, he is feeling better about the Chiefs, especially since the arrival of Dwayne Bowe, the developing wide receiver from Louisiana State university. While a “hater-at-heart”, Paul truly  loves his wife, kids and grandkids with unspeakable joy and admiration.  And sometimes he even goes to church at Mount Pleasant.  But, not enough to believe in the Chiefs this week. Seattle by 7

Carl Clark: Is really thankful for he will celebrate his 51st wedding anniversary on Friday. Thus, he has ceaseless admiration for his wife and family.  And as for the Chiefs, they ought to be thankful that they have Jamaal Charles, who has had five 100-yard-plus rushing games. Carl also believes those extra- long practice sessions helped the Chiefs regain their AFC West lead. No longer a hater. Chiefs by 3

Congressman Bubba Cleaver:  man of the cloth, he is so thankful to have a “fabulous” family and an “unusally high” number of friends and supporters, And he says the Chiefs should thank God for the best, complementary running-back duo in the NFL...Charles and Jones. After Sunday’s victory, Rev. is moving away from Ike and Booker’s influence and standing on his own. Chiefs by 6

Issac Gardner, Jr.:  Yes, Ike was named after his “Chef-on-the-train” dad.  Now deceased, Mr. Gardner would often cook wild-game dinners for us guys and our families.  Thus, Ike is thankful for God and his family. And while still mad at the Chiefs for now over 40 years, he says they should be thankful for two-time, All-Pro, Brian Waters.  Now in his 11th season, Waters has lent stability to a “sometimey” offensive line.  But, that’s not enough for Ike to reduce his “hating”. Seattle by 10

Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd is thankful for “life”, in general.  Certainly he includes his family and his many friends  in that statement.  And a month ago, he veered from his usual mild-manners and chided Dwayne Bowe for his mediocre play,  Now he apologizes after seeing Bowe operate these last few games, especially against Arizona and Denver. Because of his prolific fair-mindedness, most folks refer to Lloyd as a “gentleman’s gentleman”. Chiefs by 7

Ollie Hubbard: You remember last week, Ollie went on and on about his “earth angel” wife, Sandra.  And it wasn’t even Thanksgiving.  But, this week he is adding  to his list his two “classy” daughters and his brilliant granddaughter, Karrington. Plus, the many who depend on him for local and national news.  And like Lloyd, he, too, feels Bowe has arrived and just might make All-Pro, Especially if the Chiefs luck up and win the West. . . Keep being thankful, Ollie. Chiefs by 3

Jim Nunnelly: Feels that the Chiefs defense, led by Tamba Hali, is grossly over-looked. Hali is only second to Derrick Thomas and Neil Smith, when it comes to forcing fumbles.  And yes, look for the fifth year linebacker to be All-Pro this year.  Personally, Grand Dad is thankful for his wife, two adult children and the five grandchildren (who have made major career decisions this year).  And he also is thankful for the Call, the Carter Broadcast Group and Swope Health Services for standing behind the teenagers in our city. And he looks for Hali and the Rockets to stop Seattle cold. Chiefs by 14

Ed West: Wouldn’t you know that this computer genius would make his wife and family, along with his health, as his most-thankful-for part of his life?  That’s well-rounded Ed. And while each of us picked a Chiefs’ player, Ed selected Romeo Crennel, the defensive coordinator.  Ed says the Chiefs were just lucky to have landed a defensive leader who has been to the Super Bowl five times, in various capacities.  So, Ed is full of thanks and geeky information. . . .and surely believes Kansas City will win its seventh game against Seattle. Chiefs by 10

Final note:  This week, being Thanksgiving and all, we are certainly thankful for the Call and their staff, and to each of you for allowing us to be a part of your life, especially during the football season.  For over 40 years now, we have gathered each Monday night and discussed the ways of the world, our families, and occasionally football.  Never has it been entirely about football, though we each love the game. Really, it has always been about friendship, camaraderie and good, clean fun.  And as mad as we might make each other sometimes, we have never gone home angry or unforgiven.
Again, thanks to each of you and especially Lisa Page for reminding all of us to be thankful everyday, not just on Thanksgiving.

Chiefs by 10Paul Booker: Fresh from celebrating his two birthdays, Booker is thankful that he hasn’t been run out of town for his many disloyal predictions, against the Chiefs.  However, he is feeling better about the Chiefs, especially since the arrival of Dwayne Bowe, the developing wide receiver from Louisiana State university. While a “hater-at-heart”, Paul truly  loves his wife, kids and grandkids with unspeakable joy and admiration.  And sometimes he even goes to church at Mount Pleasant.  But, not enough to believe in the Chiefs this week. Seattle by 7Carl Clark: Is really thankful for he will celebrate his 51st wedding anniversary on Friday. Thus, he has ceaseless admiration for his wife and family.  And as for the Chiefs, they ought to be thankful that they have Jamaal Charles, who has had five 100-yard-plus rushing games. Carl also believes those extra- long practice sessions helped the Chiefs regain their AFC West lead. No longer a hater. Chiefs by 3Congressman Bubba Cleaver:  man of the cloth, he is so thankful to have a “fabulous” family and an “unusally high” number of friends and supporters, And he says the Chiefs should thank God for the best, complementary running-back duo in the NFL...Charles and Jones. After Sunday’s victory, Rev. is moving away from Ike and Booker’s influence and standing on his own. Chiefs by 6Issac Gardner, Jr.:  Yes, Ike was named after his “Chef-on-the-train” dad.  Now deceased, Mr. Gardner would often cook wild-game dinners for us guys and our families.  Thus, Ike is thankful for God and his family. And while still mad at the Chiefs for now over 40 years, he says they should be thankful for two-time, All-Pro, Brian Waters.  Now in his 11th season, Waters has lent stability to a “sometimey” offensive line.  But, that’s not enough for Ike to reduce his “hating”. Seattle by 10 Lloyd Greenfield: Lloyd is thankful for “life”, in general.  Certainly he includes his family and his many friends  in that statement.  And a month ago, he veered from his usual mild-manners and chided Dwayne Bowe for his mediocre play,  Now he apologizes after seeing Bowe operate these last few games, especially against Arizona and Denver. Because of his prolific fair-mindedness, most folks refer to Lloyd as a “gentleman’s gentleman”. Chiefs by 7Ollie Hubbard: You remember last week, Ollie went on and on about his “earth angel” wife, Sandra.  And it wasn’t even Thanksgiving.  But, this week he is adding  to his list his two “classy” daughters and his brilliant granddaughter, Karrington. Plus, the many who depend on him for local and national news.  And like Lloyd, he, too, feels Bowe has arrived and just might make All-Pro, Especially if the Chiefs luck up and win the West. . . Keep being thankful, Ollie. Chiefs by 3Jim Nunnelly: Feels that the Chiefs defense, led by Tamba Hali, is grossly over-looked. Hali is only second to Derrick Thomas and Neil Smith, when it comes to forcing fumbles.  And yes, look for the fifth year linebacker to be All-Pro this year.  Personally, Grand Dad is thankful for his wife, two adult children and the five grandchildren (who have made major career decisions this year).  And he also is thankful for the Call, the Carter Broadcast Group and Swope Health Services for standing behind the teenagers in our city. And he looks for Hali and the Rockets to stop Seattle cold. Chiefs by 14Ed West: Wouldn’t you know that this computer genius would make his wife and family, along with his health, as his most-thankful-for part of his life?  That’s well-rounded Ed. And while each of us picked a Chiefs’ player, Ed selected Romeo Crennel, the defensive coordinator.  Ed says the Chiefs were just lucky to have landed a defensive leader who has been to the Super Bowl five times, in various capacities.  So, Ed is full of thanks and geeky information. . . .and surely believes Kansas City will win its seventh game against Seattle. Chiefs by 10  Final note:  This week, being Thanksgiving and all, we are certainly thankful for the Call and their staff, and to each of you for allowing us to be a part of your life, especially during the football season.  For over 40 years now, we have gathered each Monday night and discussed the ways of the world, our families, and occasionally football.  Never has it been entirely about football, though we each love the game. Really, it has always been about friendship, camaraderie and good, clean fun.  And as mad as we might make each other sometimes, we have never gone home angry or unforgiven. Again, thanks to each of you and especially Lisa Page for reminding all of us to be thankful everyday, not just on Thanksgiving.

paragraphs.text: Monday Niters
Johnny Cash, Memorable Ministers And The Chiefs

frames.text: Monday NitersJohnny Cash, Memorable Ministers And The Chiefs

paragraphs.text: About 50 years ago, Johnny Cash recorded a song, called, “A Boy Named Sue”.

Well, the Chiefs are going to face a “Man Called Suh”. He was last year’s  “Defensive Rookie Of The Year” in the NFL. His complete name is Ndamudong Suh (pronounced N dam u kong). This unusual name is African and it means “house of spears”. He is 6’4” tall and hails from Portland, Oregon. That where his Cameroon-born father and Jamaica-born mother resides.

What does that have to do with the Chiefs? Well, the paper-thin, Chiefs’ offense will have to face Ndamukong Suh and the rest of the Detroit Lions on Sunday. It’s at noon and you can look for this man named “Suh” to be all over  and all in the Chiefs’ backfield, just throwing Peanut Brittle Matt Cassel and Once In A While Jamal Charles all over the place.
Not bad for a boy named “Sue”.

Well, we Monday Niters met over at Ike’s house and had some show-stopping cherry cobbler. Though he didn’t prepare the multi-faceted meal, he walked around kingly, like he was part of it. Truth is his wife, their daughter Shelly and her daughter Danielle prepared every dish and yet, Cantankerous Ike tried to take credit for such a culinary display. A minister would have concluded that he is richly blessed. Speaking of ministers, that was the main topic of our conversations. Here goes, along with our predictions.

Dr. Charles Allen: He remembered Rev. John Williams at the St. Stephen Baptist church. But, he also praised Father Benedict Justice, one of the few black Catholic priests in Kansas City in the ‘40s and ‘50s. But reluctantly and against all religions, he believes in the locals. Chiefs by 3

The Apostle Paul Booker:  He praised the Reverend Henderson Bell, his home-church pastor. He considers his pastor as the most approachable minister in town. But Paul doesn’t believe in The Chiefs at all. Detroit by 14

Carl “Righteous Bro-ther” Clark: He was married at the Mason Memorial in Kansas 50 two years ago. But, he has always attended St. James, under Rev. Cleaver, the only minister he has ever known. And he doesn’t know the Chiefs anymore, either. Detroit by 14

Ike “One Mean PaPaw” Gardner: Ike is so spoiled by a group of waitresses at a popular restaurant that he sometimes forgets that he is not a priest of man of the cloth. But he does remember being forced to go to church at Ward’s Chapel, years ago.  Since then, he has bonded with Rev. Cleaver and now is an unforced member of St. James. Like him or not, he says no. Detroit by 20

Lloyd “Gentleman” Greenfield: Right off, Lloyd remembered Reverend Chapelle of the Second Baptist Church, as a minister who could related to young black males. Awesome man. But still sticking with the locals. Chiefs by 7

Congressman Emanuel “Bubba” Cleaver II: Being a minister himself, Cleaver had several ministers on his praise list. . .Reverends A.L. Johnson, John Preciphs, Emanuel Newton, John Eason. Isaiah Henderson Sr. and many others. But he got carried away and also praised the Chiefs. Chiefs by 8

Jim “GrandDad” Nunnelly: He praised Rev. Earl Abel for his excellence as a pastor and a friend.  Also for mentoring and selecting the very capable Reverend Leonard Butler as his successor. A good pick for Kansas City. Chiefs by 7

Ed “Mentor Man” West: Besides being a computer guru, Ed spends his time, mentoring young males over at Raytown High school.  He is so good at it that he sometimes is referred to as a minister. Not so but his hero is Reverend Cleaver ever since he came here from Osawatomie,  Kas. No religion for the Chiefs. Detroit by 40

Ollie “Barbara Walters” Hubbard: Ollie knows everybody and everything. He reached way back to choose Reverend D.A. Holmes as his most memorable minister, a namesake for elderly homes and a school. But still believes the Chiefs will get a good education Sunday. Detroit by 40
